Using a coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex…)? Copy the prompt below and paste it in the agent's chat, from your app's root folder. It guides the agent through installing and configuring the library for the features you choose, and tells it which values it must ask you for instead of guessing. You can also save it as AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md content so the agent keeps it as context. tip Use the copy button in the top right corner of the block. Prompt You are setting up the React Native library `react-native-oauth-essentials` in this app. Docs: https://lucaswitch.github.io/react-native-oauth-essentials/docs/intro Exact API reference: https://lucaswitch.github.io/react-native-oauth-essentials/docs/methods ## Rules - Never invent values. Ask me for anything you cannot read from the project: OAuth client ids, domains, backend URLs, Apple Team ID. Use clearly named placeholders (e.g. `YOUR_IOS_CLIENT_ID`) only if I tell you to continue without them. - Never put client secrets in the app. - Only configure the features I choose. Do not touch unrelated native config. - Show me every native file you change (Info.plist, entitlements, AndroidManifest.xml, Podfile, app.json). - At the end, list what I still have to do outside the code (consoles, servers, real device tests). ## Step 0: inspect the project and ask me 1. Detect the package manager (yarn / npm / pnpm / bun), the React Native version, and whether it is bare React Native or Expo. 2. The library is a TurboModule and only works with the **New Architecture** enabled (`newArchEnabled=true` in `android/gradle.properties`, `RCT_NEW_ARCH_ENABLED=1` / default on iOS; it is the default since RN 0.76). Check it. 3. Expo: it is **not** supported in Expo Go (Expo Go only contains the Expo SDK native code; importing the library there throws an error saying so); it needs a development build (`npx expo run:ios|android`, or `eas build --profile development`). Do the native config with the library's config plugin in `app.json` (`["react-native-oauth-essentials", { "google": true | { "iosClientId", "webClientId" }, "appleSignIn": true, "webCredentialsDomains": ["<domain>"] }]`, only the keys of the chosen features) instead of editing the generated `ios/` / `android/` folders: see https://lucaswitch.github.io/react-native-oauth-essentials/docs/expo. `google: true` reads the ids from the Firebase files set in `ios.googleServicesFile` / `android.googleServicesFile`. Any Android change below that is not in the plugin (custom redirect intent filter) is lost when `android/` is regenerated, so tell me about it. 4. Read the iOS bundle identifier (Xcode project / `app.json`) and the Android `applicationId` (`android/app/build.gradle`). 5. Ask me which features I want: Google, Apple, saved passwords, passkeys, generic OAuth/OpenID Connect provider, hybrid sign in (one picker with the credentials the user already has, for app start). ## Step 1: install 1. Install `react-native-oauth-essentials` with the project's package manager. 2. iOS: `cd ios && pod install` (or `bundle exec pod install` if there is a Gemfile). 3. Android: nothing to link. Minimum SDK is 24. The library manifest already registers its `CustomTabsActivity`. ## Step 2: Google (if chosen) First check for Firebase config files (`GoogleService-Info.plist`, `google-services.json`): when Google is enabled in Firebase Authentication (with the SHA-1 added to the Firebase Android app), Firebase creates the OAuth clients and the files contain the ids (`CLIENT_ID` / `REVERSED_CLIENT_ID` in the plist; `client_type` 3 = web in the json). Otherwise ask me for the client ids. They come from Google Cloud Console > APIs & Services > Credentials, all in the same project: - **Web client id**: `webClientId`. Android passes it to Credential Manager; iOS uses it as the default `serverClientId` (idToken audience and `serverAuthCode`). - **Android client id**: never passed in code, but must exist with the `applicationId` and the SHA-1 of every signing key (debug, release, and the Play App Signing key). Get debug/release SHA-1 with `cd android && ./gradlew signingReport` and show them to me. - **iOS client id**: created with the iOS bundle id. It is the `iosClientId` (a web client id does not work as the iOS client id). Prefer putting the ids in the app config, so the code calls `googleSignIn()` without client ids. Expo: the plugin's `google` option does all of it (`true` with the Firebase files, or `{ iosClientId, webClientId }`). Bare React Native: iOS config: the reversed iOS client id (split by `.`, reversed, joined) must be a URL scheme in `ios/<App>/Info.plist` (always, even with Firebase: it is `REVERSED_CLIENT_ID`). If it is missing, `googleSignIn` / `googleSilentSignIn` reject with `CONFIGURATION_ERROR` and the error `message` has the exact scheme to add. Also add `GIDClientID` (iOS client id) and `GIDServerClientID` (web client id); without `GIDClientID`, iOS reads `CLIENT_ID` of a `GoogleService-Info.plist` in the app target. ```xml <key>CFBundleURLTypes</key> <array> <dict> <key>CFBundleURLSchemes</key> <array> <!-- 1234-abcd.apps.googleusercontent.com becomes: --> <string>com.googleusercontent.apps.1234-abcd</string> </array> </dict> </array> ``` Merge with an existing `CFBundleURLTypes` array instead of adding a second key. Android config: add the **web** client id inside `<application>` of `android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` (not needed when the app applies the Firebase `google-services` Gradle plugin with `google-services.json`, which generates `default_web_client_id`): ```xml <meta-data android:name="com.oauthessentials.GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID" android:value="WEB_CLIENT_ID" /> ``` Code: ```ts import { googleSignIn, CredentialsType } from 'react-native-oauth-essentials'; // Ids read from the app config. Alternative: googleSignIn({ iosClientId, webClientId }, options) // (iOS uses iosClientId + webClientId as serverClientId, Android uses webClientId). const result = await googleSignIn({ mode: 'button', // Android: use 'button' when the user taps a "Sign in with Google" button // nonce, hostedDomain, scopes, offlineAccess: see the docs, behavior differs per platform }); if (result.type === CredentialsType.GOOGLE_ID) { // send result.data.idToken to the backend; use the token's `sub` as the user id // (result.data.id is the Google id on iOS but the email on Android) } ``` Also wire `googleSilentSignIn()` on app start to restore the session (rejects with `NO_SIGN_IN_AVAILABLE` when there is none) and `signOut()` on logout. ## Step 3: Apple (if chosen) iOS (native): - Add the **Sign in with Apple** capability: an entitlements file with `com.apple.developer.applesignin` = `["Default"]`, referenced by `CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS` in the target (Expo: the plugin's `appleSignIn: true`). Tell me to enable it on the App ID in the Apple Developer portal. - Apple only sends `email` and `fullName` on the **first** authorization. The library keeps them in memory only, so send them to the backend right away. - On app start, call `getAppleIdCredentialState(user)` and sign out locally when it is not `AUTHORIZED`. Also register `addAppleIdCredentialRevokedListener`. - Pass `{ nonce }` (SHA-256 of a raw nonce when using Firebase/Supabase). Android (web flow, needs a backend): - `appleSignIn(androidWebUrl)` opens `androidWebUrl` in a Custom Tab. The backend runs Sign in with Apple for web (Services ID) and must finish by redirecting to `<applicationId>://oauth/callback` (the exported `OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI`), with whatever the app needs in the query. The result is `WEB_APPLE_ID` with that url. - `options` are ignored on Android: put the nonce/state in `androidWebUrl`. - Ask me for the backend URL. If there is no backend, tell me Apple on Android is not possible without one; do not build a fake flow. ## Step 4: saved passwords (if chosen) - `getPassword()` shows the passwords saved for the app. On both platforms it resolves `CANCELLED` when the user dismisses it or there is no saved password (it never resolves `false`). - iOS: needs the `webcredentials:<domain>` Associated Domain (see passkeys) for iOS to match saved passwords. - `passwordSignIn(username, password)` only **saves** a password, it does not authenticate. On iOS it does nothing: set `textContentType="username"` / `"password"` / `"newPassword"` (and `autoComplete`) on the inputs instead. - Gate the UI with `PASSWORD_SUPPORTED` (on Android it is false without Google Play Services, which the methods need). ## Step 5: passkeys (if chosen) Ask me for the relying party domain (the `rp.id`, e.g. `example.com`). The server generates the WebAuthn options and verifies the responses; the app only forwards JSON. - iOS 16+: add the Associated Domains capability with `webcredentials:<domain>` to the entitlements (Expo: the plugin's `webCredentialsDomains`). Tell me the server must serve `https://<domain>/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` with `{"webcredentials":{"apps":["<TEAM_ID>.<bundle id>"]}}`. - Android 9+: tell me the server must serve `https://<domain>/.well-known/assetlinks.json` with the `delegate_permission/common.handle_all_urls` and `delegate_permission/common.get_login_creds` relations for the `applicationId` and the SHA-256 of every signing key (`./gradlew signingReport`). - Code: `createPassKey({ requestJson })` to register and `getPassKey({ requestJson })` to sign in, where `requestJson` is the server's options JSON string; send `result.data` (a JSON string) back to the server. On iOS, `getPassKey({ requestJson, mediation: 'autofill' })` shows passkeys in the keyboard of a `textContentType="username"` input; call `cancelPassKeyAutoFill()` when that screen unmounts. - Gate the UI with `PASSKEYS_SUPPORTED`. ## Step 6: generic OAuth / OpenID Connect (if chosen) Ask me for the provider's authorization endpoint, client id, scopes, and whether the code is exchanged by the backend (recommended) or on the device (only for public clients with PKCE; never with a client secret). - Redirect URI: use the exported `OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI` (`<bundle id, lowercased>://oauth/callback` on iOS, `<applicationId>://oauth/callback` on Android) and tell me to register both exactly in the provider. - iOS needs no Info.plist change for it. - Android: the library already handles that URI. For a custom `redirectUri`, add an intent filter for it to the library activity in the app manifest (declare `xmlns:tools="http://schemas.android.com/tools"` on `<manifest>`): ```xml <activity android:name="com.oauthessentials.CustomTabsActivity" tools:node="merge"> <intent-filter> <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" /> <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" /> <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" /> <data android:scheme="my.custom.scheme" android:host="oauth" android:path="/callback" /> </intent-filter> </activity> ``` - Code: `oauthSignIn({ authorizationEndpoint, clientId, scopes, tokenEndpoint? })`. Without `tokenEndpoint`, send `result.data.code`, `codeVerifier` and `redirectUri` to the backend. ## Step 7: hybrid sign in (if chosen) `hybridSignIn({ authorizedAccounts: true })` on app start (Android uses the web client id from the app config, or pass `{ webClientId }` first). Providers differ: - iOS: Apple ID + saved passwords only (Google is not offered, the client id is ignored). - Android: Google + saved passwords only (needs Play Services; gate it with `HYBRID_SUPPORTED`). Treat `CANCELLED` as "show the normal sign in screen", not as an error. ## Step 8: integrate in the app Create one auth module (e.g. `src/auth/`) that wraps the calls and follows these contracts: - Dismissing any UI **resolves** `{ type: 'CANCELLED', data: null }`. Do not show an error for it. - Errors reject with `error.code` from `CredentialError`. Narrow them in `catch` with `isCredentialError(e, CredentialError.X)` (or `isCredentialError(e)` for any library error). Handle at least: - `CONFIGURATION_ERROR` (no client id passed or in the app config, missing iOS URL scheme, invalid `redirectUri`): a setup bug, log `e.message` (it says what to fix) and do not show it as a user error; - `BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE` (iOS: app not active, Guided Access; Android: no browser), to ask the user to retry; - `NETWORK_ERROR` (`oauthSignIn` token request failed), to ask the user to retry; - `NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR` (Android without Play Services, passkeys on old OS); - `NO_SIGN_IN_AVAILABLE` (nothing to restore / no account); - `SIMULTANEOUS_CALL_ERROR` (iOS: the same flow is already open; disable the button while pending). - In development, the library logs a `console.warn` when an option has no effect on the current platform. Do not silence it; remove the option or make it platform specific. - Always verify tokens on the backend (Google `idToken`, Apple `idToken`/`authorizationCode`). - Optional analytics: `addCredentialSuccessListener` / `addCredentialFailureListener`. Remove subscriptions on unmount. ## Step 9: verify 1. Run the project's typecheck and lint. If the project has Jest tests, add `jest.mock('react-native-oauth-essentials', () => require('react-native-oauth-essentials/jest'));` to the Jest setup file (`setupFiles`) so tests do not fail with a `native module "OauthEssentials" was not found` error, and run them. 2. Build iOS (`npx react-native run-ios` or `xcodebuild`) and Android (`cd android && ./gradlew assembleDebug`) and fix build errors. If the app throws `native module "OauthEssentials" was not found`, the binary was not rebuilt after installing (reloading Metro is not enough) or the New Architecture is off. 3. Report what you could not verify and what I must do by hand: console setup, SHA fingerprints, server files (apple-app-site-association, assetlinks.json, Apple web flow), and testing on real devices. Google on Android needs a device/emulator with Google Play; passkeys need a real device or an emulator with a Google account and screen lock.

Every error the library can produce: the codes the promises reject with, which method rejects with which code, the errors without a code and the warnings shown in development.

Cancellation is not an error. When the user dismisses the UI, methods resolve { type: 'CANCELLED', data: null } (CancelledCredentialResult). Errors reject with an Error that has a code from CredentialError and the native error text in message (OauthEssentialsError). Check the code with isCredentialError instead of reading error.code on unknown. message is meant for logs: it comes from the OS or the provider, may change between versions and is not translated. import { googleSignIn, isCredentialError, CredentialError, CredentialsType } from 'react-native-oauth-essentials'; async function signInWithGoogle() { try { const result = await googleSignIn({ mode: 'button' }); if (result.type === CredentialsType.CANCELLED) return; // the user closed the UI await api.signInWithGoogle(result.data.idToken); } catch (e) { if (!isCredentialError(e)) throw e; switch (e.code) { case CredentialError.CONFIGURATION_ERROR: console.error(e.message); // a bug in the app setup, the message says what to fix break; case CredentialError.NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR: showMessage('Update Google Play Services to sign in with Google.'); break; case CredentialError.NO_SIGN_IN_AVAILABLE: showMessage('Add a Google account to this device to continue.'); break; case CredentialError.BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE: showMessage('Could not open the sign in page. Try again.'); break; default: report(e.code, e.message); showMessage('Sign in failed. Try again.'); } } }

Code Platform Meaning Usual handling CONFIGURATION_ERROR Both The app is misconfigured Fix the setup (the message says what is missing) NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR Both The device, OS version or platform does not support the method Hide the option, or ask to update Play Services NO_SIGN_IN_AVAILABLE Both There is no credential to return Show the normal sign in screen BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE Both The browser session could not be opened Let the user try again NO_ACTIVITY_ERROR Both No screen to present the UI from Call the method again once a screen is visible SIMULTANEOUS_CALL_ERROR iOS The same method is still waiting for a previous call Ignore it (the first call keeps going) NETWORK_ERROR Both oauthSignIn token request failed Let the user try again INVALID_RESULT_ERROR Both The provider failed or returned something unexpected Report it and let the user try again NO_PLAY_SERVICES_ERROR - Deprecated, never used Use NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR

Method CONFIGURATION NOT_SUPPORTED NO_SIGN_IN BROWSER NO_ACTIVITY SIMULTANEOUS NETWORK INVALID_RESULT googleSignIn ✓ A A i ✓ i ✓ googleSilentSignIn ✓ A ✓ A i ✓ signOut A getPassword A A i ✓ passwordSignIn A A appleSignIn A A i ✓ getAppleIdCredentialState A i hybridSignIn A A A A i ✓ createPassKey ✓ A i ✓ getPassKey ✓ A A i ✓ cancelPassKeyAutoFill oauthSignIn ✓ ✓ ✓ i ✓ ✓ The column names drop the suffixes: NO_SIGN_IN is NO_SIGN_IN_AVAILABLE, BROWSER is BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE, and so on.

addCredentialFailureListener receives { code, message } for the rejections of googleSignIn, googleSilentSignIn, getPassword, appleSignIn, hybridSignIn, createPassKey, getPassKey and the Android rejections of passwordSignIn. It is not called for: SIMULTANEOUS_CALL_ERROR; the iOS NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR below iOS 16 and the iOS missing requestJson error (passkeys); signOut, getAppleIdCredentialState, cancelPassKeyAutoFill and oauthSignIn, which never emit events.

These do not have a CredentialError code, so isCredentialError returns false for them. Error When Fix Error: "react-native-oauth-essentials does not work in Expo Go…" Thrown when the library is imported in Expo Go, which does not contain its native code Use a development build: npx expo run:ios / npx expo run:android or eas build --profile development (see Expo) Error: "the native module "OauthEssentials" was not found…" Thrown on import when the app binary does not contain the library: it was not rebuilt after installing (reloading Metro is not enough), pod install was not run, or the New Architecture is off Run pod install in ios/, rebuild the app and enable the New Architecture Rejection with code 'CANCELLED': "Module is being invalidated" Android: a pending appleSignIn / oauthSignIn browser session when the React Native instance is destroyed (e.g. a reload in development) Nothing: the JS that was waiting is gone too

In development (__DEV__) the library logs a console.warn once per method and option, prefixed with [react-native-oauth-essentials] <method>:. They do not change the result and are not shown in release builds. Warning Methods Meaning "<option>" is ignored on iOS. / on Android. googleSignIn, googleSilentSignIn, hybridSignIn, appleSignIn, oauthSignIn The option has no effect on this platform (see the Platform column in Types) the Google client id is ignored on iOS… hybridSignIn iOS hybridSignIn offers Apple ID and passwords, not Google does nothing on iOS: set textContentType on your inputs… passwordSignIn iOS has no API to save a password without an associated domain "preferImmediatelyAvailableCredentials: false" is ignored on iOS… createPassKey, getPassKey iOS modal requests only offer passkeys on the device "mediation: 'autofill'" is ignored on Android. createPassKey, getPassKey AutoFill passkeys are iOS only additionalParameters.<key> is ignored: the library sets it… oauthSignIn response_type, client_id, redirect_uri, state, code_challenge and code_challenge_method cannot be overridden

Shown by npx expo prebuild (and npx expo run:* / EAS builds) for the Expo config plugin. Message Type Meaning no Google iOS client id, so Info.plist is not changed… Warning (iOS) google is set but no iOS client id was found in the plugin options nor ios.googleServicesFile. Fine if you only use Google on Android; otherwise googleSignIn rejects with CONFIGURATION_ERROR on iOS no Google web client id, so GIDServerClientID is not set… Warning (iOS) The iOS idToken audience will be the iOS client id. Set webClientId or android.googleServicesFile if your backend expects the web client id no Google web client id: googleSignIn() rejects with CONFIGURATION_ERROR on Android… Warning (Android) Set webClientId or android.googleServicesFile AndroidManifest.xml has no <application> Error The Android project is broken; regenerate it with npx expo prebuild --clean ENOENT: no such file or directory Error ios.googleServicesFile / android.googleServicesFile points to a file that does not exist (paths are relative to the project root)

The library ships an Expo config plugin (app.plugin.js) that writes the native config for you. It is not supported in Expo Go (see why): use a development build (npx expo prebuild / npx expo run:ios / npx expo run:android, or EAS Build). The New Architecture must be enabled (the default since SDK 52).

npx expo install react-native-oauth-essentials Add the plugin to app.json (or app.config.js) with only the features you use: { "expo": { "plugins": [ [ "react-native-oauth-essentials", { "google": { "iosClientId": "1234-abcd.apps.googleusercontent.com", "webClientId": "5678-efgh.apps.googleusercontent.com" }, "appleSignIn": true, "webCredentialsDomains": ["example.com"] } ] ] } } Then regenerate the native project: npx expo prebuild (or npx expo run:ios / npx expo run:android, which run it).

All options are optional. Option Type iOS Android google true | { iosClientId?: string; webClientId?: string } Info.plist: the reversed iOS client id URL scheme in CFBundleURLTypes (not added twice), GIDClientID = iOS client id and, when a web client id is found, GIDServerClientID = web client id AndroidManifest: <meta-data android:name="com.oauthessentials.GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID"> = web client id appleSignIn boolean Entitlements: com.apple.developer.applesignin = ["Default"] Nothing webCredentialsDomains string[] Entitlements: webcredentials:<domain> for each domain in com.apple.developer.associated-domains, merged with the existing ones (used by passkeys and saved passwords) Nothing

The client ids come from the plugin options or, when missing, from the Firebase config files set in the Expo config. Ids passed to the plugin win over the files. iOS client id: written with its URL scheme, which is the client id split by ., reversed and joined: 1234-abcd.apps.googleusercontent.com becomes com.googleusercontent.apps.1234-abcd. When none is found, prebuild only warns and leaves Info.plist unchanged (fine if you use Google on Android only), and Google Sign-In on iOS rejects with CONFIGURATION_ERROR unless you pass { iosClientId } in code. Web client id: prebuild only warns when none is found. Android sign in then rejects with CONFIGURATION_ERROR (unless you pass { webClientId } in code), and the iOS idToken audience is the iOS client id. Because the ids are in Info.plist and AndroidManifest, the native side reads them from there, so call the methods without client ids: import { googleSignIn } from 'react-native-oauth-essentials'; const result = await googleSignIn(); // or googleSignIn({ mode: 'button' }) Passing { iosClientId, webClientId } in code also works and wins over the config. See Google Sign-In and the Google OAuth setup to create the client ids.

With Firebase, set google: true and point the Expo config to the Firebase files: the plugin reads the ids from them. { "expo": { "ios": { "bundleIdentifier": "com.example.app", "googleServicesFile": "./GoogleService-Info.plist" }, "android": { "package": "com.example.app", "googleServicesFile": "./google-services.json" }, "plugins": [["react-native-oauth-essentials", { "google": true }]] } } ios.googleServicesFile: CLIENT_ID is the iOS client id. android.googleServicesFile (google-services.json): the web client id is the OAuth client with client_type 3, and the iOS client id (when the plist does not give one) is the client_type 2 client whose ios_info.bundle_id matches ios.bundleIdentifier. When Google is enabled as a sign-in provider in Firebase Authentication (and the SHA-1 is added to the Firebase Android app), Firebase creates the web, Android and iOS OAuth clients itself; download the config files again after that so they contain the ids.
Adds the Sign in with Apple entitlement. You still need to enable Sign in with Apple on the App ID in the Apple Developer portal (EAS Build can sync capabilities for you). See Apple Sign-In.

Adds webcredentials: Associated Domains, needed by passkeys and for iOS to match saved passwords. Your server must still serve https://<domain>/.well-known/apple-app-site-association (and assetlinks.json for Android passkeys).

Google needs the web client id, written by the google option as manifest meta-data (or passed in code). The Android client id is never used directly: it only has to exist in Google Cloud with your package name and SHA-1 fingerprints. The library manifest already registers the CustomTabsActivity that handles OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI (<applicationId>://oauth/callback).

Expo Go is a prebuilt app from the stores that only contains the native modules of the Expo SDK. Your JavaScript is loaded into it, but native code (the library's Swift and Kotlin, the GoogleSignIn SDK) cannot be added at runtime, and its URL schemes, entitlements and bundle id belong to Expo Go, not to your app. Use a development build (npx expo run:ios / npx expo run:android or eas build --profile development). In Expo Go, importing the library throws: react-native-oauth-essentials does not work in Expo Go, which only contains the Expo SDK native code. Create a development build instead: `npx expo run:ios` / `npx expo run:android` or `eas build --profile development`.

documents.t: This guide will walk you through setting up Google OAuth for your React Native app on both iOS and Android.
A Google Cloud Console account Your React Native app's bundle identifier (iOS) and package name (Android)
Go to Google Cloud Console Create a new project or select an existing one Navigate to APIs & Services → Credentials

Click OAuth consent screen in the left sidebar Select External (or Internal if using Google Workspace) Fill in the required information: App name User support email Developer contact information Add scopes (at minimum): openid profile email Save and continue

You need to create THREE different OAuth client IDs for your app: Using Firebase? When Google is enabled as a sign-in provider in Firebase Authentication and the SHA-1 fingerprints are added to the Firebase Android app, Firebase creates the web, Android and iOS OAuth clients for you. Download GoogleService-Info.plist and google-services.json again afterwards: they contain the ids, and the library can read them (see Step 4). You can skip to Step 4.

This is the webClientId in your React Native code: Android passes it to Credential Manager, and iOS uses it as the default serverClientId (the idToken audience your backend verifies, and serverAuthCode). Click Create Credentials → OAuth client ID Select Web application Name it (e.g., "My App - Web Client") No need to add Authorized redirect URIs Click Create Copy the Client ID - it is your webClientId

Click Create Credentials → OAuth client ID Select iOS Name it (e.g., "My App - iOS") Enter your iOS Bundle ID (e.g., com.yourcompany.yourapp) Find this in your Info.plist or Xcode project settings Click Create Copy the iOS Client ID - it is your iosClientId, and its reversed form is the iOS URL scheme

Click Create Credentials → OAuth client ID Select Android Name it (e.g., "My App - Android") Enter your Android Package name (e.g., com.yourcompany.yourapp) Find this in android/app/build.gradle under applicationId Enter your SHA-1 certificate fingerprint. Create one Android client per signing key: debug, release (upload) and the Play App Signing key (Play Console > Setup > App signing), or Google Sign-In fails in the Play Store build. cd android && ./gradlew signingReport prints the debug and release fingerprints: For Development (Debug): # macOS/Linux keytool -list -v -keystore ~/.android/debug.keystore -alias androiddebugkey -storepass android -keypass android # Windows keytool -list -v -keystore %USERPROFILE%\.android\debug.keystore -alias androiddebugkey -storepass android -keypass android For Production (Release): keytool -list -v -keystore /path/to/your/release.keystore -alias your-key-alias Click Create You never pass the Android Client ID in code. Google only checks that one exists for your package name and signature

In the app config (recommended). Put the ids in the native config (4.2, 4.3), or let the Expo config plugin write them, and call the methods without client ids: import { googleSignIn } from 'react-native-oauth-essentials'; const credential = await googleSignIn(); // or googleSignIn({ mode: 'button' }) When the client id is not passed, each platform reads it in this order: iOS client id: GIDClientID in Info.plist, then CLIENT_ID of the Firebase GoogleService-Info.plist bundled in the app. serverClientId (idToken audience): the serverClientId option, then webClientId, then GIDServerClientID in Info.plist. Android web client id: the com.oauthessentials.GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID meta-data of AndroidManifest.xml, then the default_web_client_id string generated by the Firebase google-services Gradle plugin from google-services.json. When none is found, the call rejects with CONFIGURATION_ERROR and the message lists these sources. In code. Pass { iosClientId, webClientId }; each platform picks the id it needs, and a passed id wins over the config: const GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS = { iosClientId: 'YOUR_IOS_CLIENT_ID.apps.googleusercontent.com', webClientId: 'YOUR_WEB_CLIENT_ID.apps.googleusercontent.com', }; const credential = await googleSignIn(GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS); iOS uses iosClientId and webClientId as the default serverClientId. Android uses webClientId. Either id can be omitted to read only that one from the config. A single string still works, but it is used as is: it must be the iOS client id on iOS and the web client id on Android. The Android client id is never passed.

You need to add a URL scheme to your iOS app's Info.plist file: the iOS client id split by ., reversed and joined (it is REVERSED_CLIENT_ID in Firebase's GoogleService-Info.plist). It is required even when the client id comes from GoogleService-Info.plist. With Expo, the config plugin google option does it for you. When the scheme is missing, googleSignIn and googleSilentSignIn reject with CONFIGURATION_ERROR and the error message contains the exact scheme to add. Location: ios/YourAppName/Info.plist Add the following configuration: <key>CFBundleURLTypes</key> <array> <dict> <key>CFBundleTypeRole</key> <string>Editor</string> <key>CFBundleURLSchemes</key> <array> <!-- This is your iOS Client ID in reverse notation --> <string>com.googleusercontent.apps.YOUR_IOS_CLIENT_ID</string> </array> </dict> </array> Info.plist Generator​ Use this tool to generate the correct Info.plist entry: Info.plist Entry Generator iOS Client ID: Generate Info.plist Entry Copy this to your Info.plist: Copy to Clipboard Manual Steps:​ Open ios/YourAppName/Info.plist in Xcode or text editor Find the <dict> section (usually near the top) Add the generated CFBundleURLTypes configuration Replace YOUR_IOS_CLIENT_ID with your actual iOS Client ID (without the .apps.googleusercontent.com part) Example: If your iOS Client ID is: 1234567890-abcdefghijklmnop.apps.googleusercontent.com Your reversed URL scheme should be: com.googleusercontent.apps.1234567890-abcdefghijklmnop To call googleSignIn() without client ids, add them to Info.plist too (or add the Firebase GoogleService-Info.plist to the app target, which gives the iOS client id but not GIDServerClientID): <key>GIDClientID</key> <string>1234567890-abcdefghijklmnop.apps.googleusercontent.com</string> <key>GIDServerClientID</key> <string>YOUR_WEB_CLIENT_ID.apps.googleusercontent.com</string>

To call googleSignIn() without client ids, add the web client id to android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml, inside <application>: <application> <meta-data android:name="com.oauthessentials.GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID" android:value="YOUR_WEB_CLIENT_ID.apps.googleusercontent.com" /> </application> With Firebase, the google-services Gradle plugin already generates the default_web_client_id string from google-services.json, which the library reads when the meta-data is missing. Nothing else to add to the native project. Make sure: You use the Web client id (not the Android one), in the config or as webClientId You created the Android OAuth client ID in Google Cloud Console You added the SHA-1 of every signing key, including Play App Signing Your package name matches
Open Xcode Select your target → Info tab Expand "URL Types" You should see your reversed client ID as a URL scheme
Run your app on an Android device/emulator Make sure Google Play Services is installed and updated Test the sign-in flow

The message says what is missing: the iOS client id (pass iosClientId, set GIDClientID or add GoogleService-Info.plist to the app target) or the exact URL scheme to add to CFBundleURLSchemes Make sure iosClientId is the iOS client id: a web client id there produces a scheme that does not match Rebuild the iOS app after changing Info.plist (or run npx expo prebuild with Expo)

The web client id is missing: pass { webClientId }, add the com.oauthessentials.GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID meta-data or use google-services.json with the google-services Gradle plugin (the web client id, not the Android one) Rebuild the Android app after changing AndroidManifest.xml (or run npx expo prebuild with Expo)

The app binary does not contain the library: rebuild it after installing (pod install in ios/, then build again; reloading Metro is not enough) and make sure the New Architecture is enabled In Expo Go the error says the library does not work there: use a development build (see Expo)
Verify your CFBundleURLSchemes matches your reversed iOS Client ID exactly Make sure there are no typos or extra spaces Rebuild your iOS app after making changes
