documents.t: Install Google Play Services on your device/emulator Update Google Play Services to the latest version Use a device with Google Play Store (not AOSP builds)
Verify your SHA-1 certificate fingerprint is correct Make sure package name matches exactly Wait a few minutes after creating credentials (Google takes time to propagate changes)

Double-check iosClientId is the iOS client id and webClientId the Web client id Verify the client ID is copied correctly with no extra spaces Make sure the iOS/Android client IDs are created and active in Google Cloud Console

Never commit client IDs to public repositories Use environment variables or config files (added to .gitignore) Example: .env file with GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID=... Use different credentials for development and production Create separate Google Cloud projects or OAuth clients Use different SHA-1 fingerprints for debug and release builds Verify tokens on your backend Always validate the idToken server-side See Google Identity: Authenticate with a backend server
Google Cloud Console Google Sign-In for iOS Documentation Google Sign-In for Android Documentation OAuth 2.0 Client IDs Backend Token Verification

import React from 'react'; import { Button, View, Text } from 'react-native'; import { googleSignIn, isCredentialError, GOOGLE_ID_SUPPORTED, CredentialsType, CredentialError, } from 'react-native-oauth-essentials'; // Your OAuth 2.0 client ids from Google Cloud Console const GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS = { iosClientId: 'YOUR_IOS_CLIENT_ID.apps.googleusercontent.com', webClientId: 'YOUR_WEB_CLIENT_ID.apps.googleusercontent.com', }; export default function GoogleSignInExample() { const [user, setUser] = React.useState(null); async function handleGoogleSignIn() { // Android: false without Google Play Services if (!GOOGLE_ID_SUPPORTED) { alert('Google Sign-In is not available on this device'); return; } try { const credential = await googleSignIn(GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS, { authorizedAccounts: true, // Android only autoSelectEnabled: false, // Android only }); if (credential.type === CredentialsType.GOOGLE_ID) { setUser(credential.data); console.log('User signed in:', credential.data); // Send idToken to your backend for verification await verifyWithBackend(credential.data.idToken); } else if (credential.type === CredentialsType.CANCELLED) { console.log('User cancelled sign-in'); } } catch (error) { if (isCredentialError(error, CredentialError.CONFIGURATION_ERROR)) { console.error(error.message); // setup problem: missing client id or iOS URL scheme } console.error('Google Sign-In Error:', error); alert('Sign-in failed'); } } async function verifyWithBackend(idToken: string) { try { const response = await fetch('https://yourapi.com/auth/google', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ idToken }), }); const data = await response.json(); console.log('Backend verification:', data); } catch (error) { console.error('Backend verification failed:', error); } } return ( <View style={{ padding: 20 }}> {user ? ( <View> <Text>Welcome, {user.displayName}!</Text> <Text>Email: {user.email}</Text> </View> ) : ( <Button title="Sign in with Google" onPress={handleGoogleSignIn} /> )} </View> ); }

After successfully setting up Google OAuth: Test on both iOS and Android devices Implement backend token verification Handle user data securely Set up proper error handling Consider adding other sign-in methods (Apple, Password) Need help? Check the Usage Guide for more examples.

Using a coding agent? Copy the setup prompt for AI agents and paste it in your agent to install and configure everything. Install the library via npm: npm install react-native-oauth-essentials yarn add react-native-oauth-essentials Make sure to pod install to update the native part of your app: cd ios; pod install; or // bundle exec pod install
Expo Go is not supported. Use a development build and the config plugin, which writes the native config described below (from the client ids or the Firebase files): see Expo.

Enabling Google Sign-In in your app requires three OAuth client ids, all created in the same Google Cloud project. See the Google OAuth setup guide for every step. Creating Google ID credentials in Google Cloud Console​ If you already have the credentials in hand you can skip this step. Open or create a project Open your project in the Google Cloud Console, or create a new project if you don't already have one. Complete the branding information Go to the Branding page and make sure all information is complete and accurate. Set app details Ensure your app has the following properly assigned: App Name App Logo App Homepage These values will be displayed to users on the Sign in with Google consent screen during sign-up and on the Third-party apps & services screen. Specify policy URLs Provide URLs for your app's Privacy Policy and Terms of Service. Create the client ids On the Clients page, create: Client Created with Used as Web application Nothing (no redirect URIs needed) webClientId: the client id of Android Credential Manager, and the iOS serverClientId (idToken audience, serverAuthCode) Android Package name (applicationId) + SHA-1 of every signing key: debug, release and the Play App Signing key Never passed in code. Google only checks that it exists for your package and signature iOS Bundle id iosClientId Using Firebase? Enable Google as a sign-in provider in Firebase Authentication and add your SHA-1 fingerprints to the Firebase Android app: Firebase creates the three OAuth clients for you, and its GoogleService-Info.plist / google-services.json contain the ids. Put the ids in the native config (see iOS Setup and Android Setup) and call the methods without client ids: import { googleSignIn } from 'react-native-oauth-essentials'; const result = await googleSignIn({ mode: 'button' }); // or googleSignIn() Or pass them as an object (a passed id wins over the config); each platform picks the one it needs: const GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS = { iosClientId: '1234-abcd.apps.googleusercontent.com', webClientId: '5678-efgh.apps.googleusercontent.com', }; const result = await googleSignIn(GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS, { mode: 'button' });

Google Sign-In needs the reversed iOS client id as a URL scheme: the client id split by ., reversed and joined. 1234-abcd.apps.googleusercontent.com becomes com.googleusercontent.apps.1234-abcd. Add it to ios/YOUR_APP_NAME/Info.plist (merge it with an existing CFBundleURLTypes array instead of adding a second key): <key>CFBundleURLTypes</key> <array> <dict> <key>CFBundleURLSchemes</key> <array> <string>com.googleusercontent.apps.1234-abcd</string> </array> </dict> </array> <!-- Lets you call googleSignIn() without iosClientId / webClientId on iOS --> <key>GIDClientID</key> <string>1234-abcd.apps.googleusercontent.com</string> <key>GIDServerClientID</key> <string>5678-efgh.apps.googleusercontent.com</string> When no client id is passed, iOS reads GIDClientID, then CLIENT_ID of the Firebase GoogleService-Info.plist if it is in the app target; the serverClientId falls back to webClientId, then GIDServerClientID. The URL scheme is always required (with Firebase it is REVERSED_CLIENT_ID of GoogleService-Info.plist). When the scheme or the client id is missing, googleSignIn and googleSilentSignIn reject with CONFIGURATION_ERROR and the error message says what to add (instead of crashing the app). With Expo, the plugin's google option adds the scheme and both keys.

The library manifest already registers its activities. To call googleSignIn() without client ids, add the web client id inside <application> of android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml: <meta-data android:name="com.oauthessentials.GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID" android:value="5678-efgh.apps.googleusercontent.com" /> Without it, the library uses the default_web_client_id string that the Firebase google-services Gradle plugin generates from google-services.json. With neither (and no webClientId passed), the call rejects with CONFIGURATION_ERROR. With Expo, the plugin's google option writes the meta-data. Make sure the Android client id exists with your package name and the SHA-1 of every signing key (cd android && ./gradlew signingReport). There you go, you're ready to use it!

If importing the library throws the native module "OauthEssentials" was not found, the app binary does not contain it: rebuild after installing (pod install in ios/, then build again; reloading Metro is not enough) and make sure the New Architecture is enabled. In Expo Go, the error says the library does not work there: use a development build.
To use the library in Jest tests, mock it with react-native-oauth-essentials/jest: see Testing with Jest.

React Native OAuth Essentials is an essential OAuth solution for React Native apps. It provides up-to-date Google Sign-In, Apple Sign-In, saved passwords, passkeys and generic OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect, delivering a native sign-in experience with a simple, promise-based API. It's a must-have for every React Native app. Platform Support: iOS and Android only. This library does not support React Native Web or other platforms.
Installation Expo config plugin (development builds; Expo Go is not supported) Setup with AI agents Testing with Jest (mock at react-native-oauth-essentials/jest) Usage

I’ve always felt that React Native lacked a single library that handles OAuth end-to-end. Most React Native apps end up downloading multiple libraries just to implement OAuth features. Each library feels different—they follow different philosophies, have different implementations, and some are outdated. Coming from native development, I wanted a library that provides all the OAuth features an app actually needs. That’s why I created and launched it as “Essentials.” One big reason is that if you include Google OAuth in your app, Apple’s App Store policies require you to provide Apple OAuth as well, or your app won’t be approved. I was frustrated going through this process myself, and seeing how much time React Native developers spent trying to deliver a “good enough” sign-in experience. So I thought—why not create one library that actually behaves and doesn’t make me want to throw my laptop out the window?
Free forever, up-to-date features, and focused only on the essentials your mobile app really needs.
Exact reference of every function exported by react-native-oauth-essentials: what it calls on each platform, what it resolves, what it rejects with and which events it emits.

Cancellation resolves. When the user dismisses the UI, methods resolve { type: 'CANCELLED', data: null } instead of rejecting (exceptions are noted per method). Errors reject with an Error that has a code from CredentialError and the native error text in message. Every code, its causes and an errors-by-method table are in Errors. Every rejection of the library has a code; narrow it with isCredentialError. Events. Credential methods also report their result through addCredentialSuccessListener / addCredentialFailureListener (see Events). Simultaneous calls (iOS). Calling a method again while its previous call is pending rejects the new call with SIMULTANEOUS_CALL_ERROR (the pending one keeps going). The locks are: googleSignIn + googleSilentSignIn, getPassword, hybridSignIn, appleSignIn, createPassKey + getPassKey, and oauthSignIn. Android has no lock, except that appleSignIn and oauthSignIn share the browser: starting one resolves the pending one as CANCELLED. Threading (iOS). Every method runs on the main thread. Development warnings. See Ignored options. Missing native module. Importing the library throws when its native code is not in the app binary: in Expo Go it says the library does not work there (use a development build), otherwise it asks to rebuild the app after installing (pod install + native build; reloading Metro is not enough) and to enable the New Architecture.

In development (__DEV__), passing an option that has no effect on the current platform logs a console.warn once per method and option: [react-native-oauth-essentials] <method>: "<option>" is ignored on <Platform>. Release builds never warn. Method iOS warns for Android warns for googleSignIn authorizedAccounts, autoSelectEnabled, mode, offlineAccess hint googleSilentSignIn authorizedAccounts, autoSelectEnabled, mode, offlineAccess, hint, scopes, nonce hint, mode hybridSignIn any client id, and every option except nonce hint, mode, scopes, offlineAccess, hostedDomain, serverClientId appleSignIn nonce, state createPassKey, getPassKey preferImmediatelyAvailableCredentials: false mediation: 'autofill' oauthSignIn prefersEphemeralSession passwordSignIn always (it does nothing on iOS)

googleSignIn, googleSilentSignIn and hybridSignIn take an optional clientId of type GoogleClientId: { iosClientId?, webClientId? } or a string. Each accepts (clientId?, options?) and (options): an object with iosClientId or webClientId is the client id, any other object is the options (null also means "no client id"). Omitted (recommended when the ids are in the app config): googleSignIn() / googleSignIn(options). The native side reads them from the app: iOS: GIDClientID in Info.plist, then CLIENT_ID of the Firebase GoogleService-Info.plist bundled in the app. serverClientId defaults to GIDServerClientID from Info.plist. Android: the com.oauthessentials.GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID <meta-data> of <application> in AndroidManifest.xml, then the default_web_client_id string generated by the Firebase google-services Gradle plugin. When none is found, rejects with CONFIGURATION_ERROR (the message lists these sources). Object: { iosClientId: IOS_CLIENT_ID, webClientId: WEB_CLIENT_ID }. A passed id wins over the config; a missing one is read from it as above. iOS uses iosClientId. webClientId is the default serverClientId (idToken audience and serverAuthCode). Android uses webClientId. String: used as is on both platforms, so it must be the iOS client id on iOS and the web client id on Android. The Expo plugin writes Info.plist and the Android meta-data from its options or the Firebase files. On iOS, before calling GoogleSignIn, the library checks that a client id exists and that the reversed client id (1234-abcd.apps.googleusercontent.com becomes com.googleusercontent.apps.1234-abcd) is in CFBundleURLTypes > CFBundleURLSchemes. Otherwise it rejects with CONFIGURATION_ERROR (the message has the exact scheme to add) instead of letting GoogleSignIn crash the app. See Installation or the Expo plugin.

Shows the Google sign in UI and resolves with the signed in account. iOS Resolves the client ids (see Google client ids) and rejects with CONFIGURATION_ERROR when there is no iOS client id or its URL scheme is not in Info.plist. Configures GoogleSignIn with the iOS client id, plus serverClientId and hostedDomain. Rejects with BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE if Guided Access is on. If the app is not active, waits up to 2 seconds for it to become active, then rejects with BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE. Finds the top most view controller attached to a window (rejects with NO_ACTIVITY_ERROR when there is none) and rejects with BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE when its window is not in the foreground (e.g. Control Center is open). Calls GIDSignIn.signIn(withPresenting:hint:additionalScopes:nonce:), which opens an ASWebAuthenticationSession. "Unable to open Safari." errors are reported as BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE. Android Rejects with CONFIGURATION_ERROR without a web client id (passed or in the app config), NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR without Google Play Services and NO_ACTIVITY_ERROR without an activity. mode: 'bottomSheet' (default): Credential Manager GetGoogleIdOption with authorizedAccounts, autoSelectEnabled and nonce. When there is no credential (no account on the device, or the sheet is in cooldown after being dismissed) and authorizedAccounts is not set, it falls back to the button flow. mode: 'button': GetSignInWithGoogleOption with nonce and hostedDomain, the full "Sign in with Google" flow (lets the user add an account). When scopes or offlineAccess are set, calls the Authorization API for that account with scopes (or openid, email, profile), hostedDomain and, with offlineAccess, requestOfflineAccess(serverClientId ?? webClientId). It may show a consent screen; declining it resolves CANCELLED. iOS Android Resolves GOOGLE_ID, CANCELLED GOOGLE_ID, CANCELLED Rejects CONFIGURATION_ERROR, BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE, NO_ACTIVITY_ERROR, SIMULTANEOUS_CALL_ERROR, INVALID_RESULT_ERROR CONFIGURATION_ERROR, NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR, NO_ACTIVITY_ERROR, NO_SIGN_IN_AVAILABLE, INVALID_RESULT_ERROR Events success / failure success / failure Options per platform Option iOS Android nonce ✅ ✅ hint ✅ ignored hostedDomain ✅ button flow and authorization only scopes requested during sign in requested in the authorization step offlineAccess no effect (serverAuthCode comes when serverClientId is set) returns serverAuthCode serverClientId idToken audience + serverAuthCode client id of the serverAuthCode mode, authorizedAccounts, autoSelectEnabled ignored ✅ Result fields that differ: id is the Google user id (sub) on iOS and the account email on Android. accessToken and grantedScopes are always set on iOS, and are null on Android unless scopes or offlineAccess were requested. phoneNumber is Android only. import { googleSignIn, isCredentialError, CredentialsType, CredentialError } from 'react-native-oauth-essentials'; try { // ids from the app config; or googleSignIn({ iosClientId, webClientId }, { mode: 'button', nonce }) const result = await googleSignIn({ mode: 'button', nonce }); if (result.type === CredentialsType.GOOGLE_ID) { await api.signInWithGoogle(result.data.idToken); } } catch (e) { if (isCredentialError(e, CredentialError.BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE)) { // ask the user to try again with the app in foreground } else if (isCredentialError(e, CredentialError.CONFIGURATION_ERROR)) { console.error(e.message); // setup bug, e.g. the missing iOS URL scheme } }

Restores a previous Google sign in. iOS: if there is no stored session, rejects with NO_SIGN_IN_AVAILABLE. Otherwise it calls GIDSignIn.restorePreviousSignIn, which never shows UI and refreshes the tokens. hint, scopes, nonce and offlineAccess are ignored, and serverAuthCode is always null. Android: GetGoogleIdOption with filterByAuthorizedAccounts and autoSelectEnabled forced on, so it signs in without UI when a single account already signed in to the app (it shows the sheet when there are several). mode is ignored. When scopes/offlineAccess are set, authorization is requested without UI. If consent would be needed, the result has accessToken: null instead of being cancelled. Resolves GOOGLE_ID or CANCELLED (user dismissed the Android sheet). Rejects with NO_SIGN_IN_AVAILABLE when there is nothing to restore, plus the same errors as googleSignIn (including CONFIGURATION_ERROR). Takes the same optional clientId. Emits success / failure events. try { const result = await googleSilentSignIn(); } catch (e) { if (isCredentialError(e, CredentialError.NO_SIGN_IN_AVAILABLE)) showSignInScreen(); }

iOS: GIDSignIn.signOut(): removes the Google session, so googleSilentSignIn rejects afterwards. It does not touch Apple ID or passwords. Android: Credential Manager clearCredentialState. It turns off auto select for every provider until the user picks an account again. Resolves true. Rejects with INVALID_RESULT_ERROR on Android when clearing fails. Does not emit events.

Shows the app's saved passwords and resolves with the one the user picks. iOS: ASAuthorizationPasswordProvider request. On iOS 16+ it only offers passwords already on the device. Resolves PASSWORD, or CANCELLED when the user dismisses it or there is no saved password. Rejects with INVALID_RESULT_ERROR on other errors and SIMULTANEOUS_CALL_ERROR. Android: Credential Manager GetPasswordOption. Resolves PASSWORD, or CANCELLED when the user dismisses it or there is no saved password. Rejects with NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR without Play Services, NO_ACTIVITY_ERROR and INVALID_RESULT_ERROR on other errors. Returns Promise<PasswordCredentialResult | CancelledCredentialResult>: it never resolves false. Emits the success event when it resolves (including CANCELLED) and the failure event when it rejects. const result = await getPassword(); if (result.type === CredentialsType.PASSWORD) { await api.signIn(result.data.username, result.data.password); } Migrating to 1.1 Before 1.1, Android resolved false when there was no password or on errors. Replace if (!result) / result === false checks with result.type === CredentialsType.CANCELLED.

Saves a username/password in the platform password manager. It does not authenticate the user against anything. iOS: does nothing and resolves false. iOS has no API to save a password without an associated domain. Use the textContentType (username, password, newPassword) props of your inputs so iOS offers to save it. Android: Credential Manager createCredential(CreatePasswordRequest), which shows the save prompt. Resolves true when saved and false on any error, including the user declining. Rejects with NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR without Play Services and NO_ACTIVITY_ERROR. Does not emit events, except the failure event for the Android rejections.

iOS: native Sign in with Apple sheet (ASAuthorizationAppleIDProvider) requesting fullName and email, with options.nonce and options.state. androidWebUrl is ignored. Resolves APPLE_ID or CANCELLED. Rejects with INVALID_RESULT_ERROR and SIMULTANEOUS_CALL_ERROR. Apple only sends email and fullName on the first authorization. This function keeps the first result of each user in memory (lost when the app is killed) and fills empty email/fullName from it. Store them on your backend. idToken and authorizationCode are null when Apple does not return them. state is options.state echoed back. Android: opens androidWebUrl in a Custom Tab. options is ignored, so put the nonce/state in your url. Your backend runs the Apple web flow and must redirect to <applicationId>://oauth/callback, the uri the library's CustomTabsActivity handles. Resolves WEB_APPLE_ID with the redirect url, scheme, host, path and query. Resolves CANCELLED when the user closes the tab or an oauthSignIn starts. Rejects with INVALID_RESULT_ERROR (missing/invalid url), NO_ACTIVITY_ERROR and BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE (no browser installed). Emits success / failure events on both platforms. const result = await appleSignIn('https://api.example.com/auth/apple', { nonce: sha256(rawNonce) });

Asks Apple, without UI, whether userId (the user of APPLE_ID) is still signed in to the app (ASAuthorizationAppleIDProvider.getCredentialState). Call it on app start and sign the user out when it is not AUTHORIZED. Resolves AUTHORIZED, REVOKED, TRANSFERRED or NOT_FOUND. Rejects with INVALID_RESULT_ERROR when the check fails. On Android it always rejects with NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR. Does not emit events. if ((await getAppleIdCredentialState(storedUserId)) !== AppleIdCredentialState.AUTHORIZED) { signOutLocally(); }

Shows a single picker with the credentials the user already has, meant for app start. The providers differ per platform: iOS: Apple ID + saved passwords. clientId is ignored, Google is not included, and only options.nonce is used (for Apple ID). On iOS 16+ only credentials already on the device are offered. Resolves APPLE_ID or PASSWORD, or CANCELLED when the user dismisses it or nothing is available. Rejects with INVALID_RESULT_ERROR and SIMULTANEOUS_CALL_ERROR. Android: Credential Manager with Google ID (GetGoogleIdOption with the web client id, authorizedAccounts, autoSelectEnabled, nonce) + saved passwords. Apple is not included, and mode, hint, scopes, offlineAccess, hostedDomain and serverClientId are ignored. Resolves GOOGLE_ID or PASSWORD, or CANCELLED. Rejects with CONFIGURATION_ERROR (no web client id passed or in the app config), NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR (no Play Services), NO_ACTIVITY_ERROR, NO_SIGN_IN_AVAILABLE and INVALID_RESULT_ERROR. Emits success / failure events. const result = await hybridSignIn({ authorizedAccounts: true }); // or hybridSignIn({ webClientId }, options)

Registers a passkey from your server's WebAuthn PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions JSON. iOS 16+: platform passkey registration. It reads challenge, rp.id, user.id, user.name, authenticatorSelection.userVerification, attestation and, on iOS 17.4+, excludeCredentials. Other fields are ignored. data is a JSON string with id, rawId, type and response.clientDataJSON / attestationObject (base64url). Rejects with NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR below iOS 16 and SIMULTANEOUS_CALL_ERROR. Android 9+: Credential Manager CreatePublicKeyCredentialRequest with the whole JSON and preferImmediatelyAvailableCredentials. data is the registration response JSON from Credential Manager. Rejects with NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR below Android 9 and NO_ACTIVITY_ERROR. Resolves PASSKEY or CANCELLED. Rejects with INVALID_RESULT_ERROR for a missing/invalid requestJson and other errors. Emits success / failure events. Send data to your server to verify it.

Signs in with a passkey from your server's WebAuthn PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions JSON. iOS 16+: platform passkey assertion. It reads challenge, rpId, allowCredentials and userVerification. mediation: 'modal' (default) shows a sheet that only offers passkeys on the device, with no "other device" QR option, so it resolves CANCELLED when there is none. Rejects with SIMULTANEOUS_CALL_ERROR while a passkey call is pending. mediation: 'autofill' shows no sheet. It waits until the user picks a passkey in the QuickType bar of a textContentType="username" field. Any later createPassKey/getPassKey call, or cancelPassKeyAutoFill(), resolves it as CANCELLED. data is a JSON string with id, rawId, type and response.clientDataJSON / authenticatorData / signature / userHandle (base64url). Rejects with NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR below iOS 16. Android 9+: Credential Manager GetPublicKeyCredentialOption with the whole JSON and preferImmediatelyAvailableCredentials. mediation is ignored. data is the authentication response JSON from Credential Manager. Rejects with NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR below Android 9, NO_ACTIVITY_ERROR and NO_SIGN_IN_AVAILABLE (no passkey). Resolves PASSKEY or CANCELLED. Rejects with INVALID_RESULT_ERROR for a missing/invalid requestJson and other errors. Emits success / failure events.

Cancels a pending getPassKey({ mediation: 'autofill' }), which then resolves (and emits) CANCELLED. Call it when the sign in screen unmounts. Resolves true when a pending AutoFill request was cancelled and false when there was none. Always resolves false on Android and below iOS 16.

Signs in with any OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect provider using the authorization code flow: Generates a random state and a PKCE S256 verifier/challenge on the native side (32 and 16 random bytes, base64url). Builds authorizationEndpoint?response_type=code&client_id=…&redirect_uri=…&state=…, plus scope (space separated) and code_challenge + code_challenge_method=S256 when usePKCE is not false. additionalParameters are added last and may override scope; response_type, client_id, redirect_uri, state, code_challenge and code_challenge_method are ignored there (with a warning in development), since the library checks or reuses them. Opens it in ASWebAuthenticationSession on iOS, with the redirectUri scheme as callback and prefersEphemeralSession. On Android it opens a Custom Tab (http/https urls only), where the redirect must reach the library's CustomTabsActivity: use OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI or add an intent filter for your uri. Reads the redirect query and fragment parameters and checks that state matches. error=access_denied resolves CANCELLED. Any other error, or a missing code, rejects. When tokenEndpoint is set, it POSTs grant_type=authorization_code, code, client_id, redirect_uri and code_verifier as application/x-www-form-urlencoded and returns the JSON response in tokens. No client secret is sent and the id_token is not validated. Resolves OAUTH with code, state, redirectUri, codeVerifier (null without PKCE), params (all redirect params) and tokens (null without tokenEndpoint). Resolves CANCELLED when the user closes the browser, the provider returns access_denied or, on Android, an appleSignIn starts. Rejects with: INVALID_RESULT_ERROR: state mismatch, provider error, no code, the token endpoint returned non 2xx (message is its error_description/error) or a non JSON response. NETWORK_ERROR: the token request failed (offline, DNS, TLS...). CONFIGURATION_ERROR: redirectUri has no scheme. BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE: iOS Guided Access, app not active within 2 seconds, its window not in the foreground, or the session could not start; Android with no browser installed. NO_ACTIVITY_ERROR (no activity on Android, no view controller in a window on iOS) and SIMULTANEOUS_CALL_ERROR (iOS). Does not emit events, not even for rejections. See OAuth Sign-In.

Called with the same { type, data } the promise resolves with, including CANCELLED. It fires for googleSignIn, googleSilentSignIn, getPassword, appleSignIn, hybridSignIn, createPassKey and getPassKey.

Called with { code, message } when one of those methods rejects (including CONFIGURATION_ERROR). These rejections are not emitted: SIMULTANEOUS_CALL_ERROR; iOS passkey NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR below iOS 16; iOS missing requestJson.

Called when iOS posts ASAuthorizationAppleIDProvider.credentialRevokedNotification, meaning the user stopped using Apple ID with the app while it is running. Never called on Android. signOut, passwordSignIn (iOS), getAppleIdCredentialState, cancelPassKeyAutoFill and oauthSignIn do not emit events. const success = addCredentialSuccessListener((event) => analytics.track('sign_in', { type: event.type })); const failure = addCredentialFailureListener((event) => analytics.track('sign_in_error', { code: event.code })); const revoked = addAppleIdCredentialRevokedListener(() => signOutLocally()); // later success.remove(); failure.remove(); revoked.remove();

Read once when the module loads. Constant iOS Android GOOGLE_PLAY_SERVICES_SUPPORTED false Play Services installed and up to date GOOGLE_ID_SUPPORTED true same as GOOGLE_PLAY_SERVICES_SUPPORTED PASSWORD_SUPPORTED true same as GOOGLE_PLAY_SERVICES_SUPPORTED APPLE_ID_SUPPORTED true true (web flow) HYBRID_SUPPORTED true same as GOOGLE_PLAY_SERVICES_SUPPORTED PASSKEYS_SUPPORTED iOS 16+ Android 9+ (API 28) OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI <bundle id, lowercased>://oauth/callback <applicationId>://oauth/callback

Type guard for a catch: returns true when error is an object whose code is a CredentialError value (and equals code when given), narrowing it to OauthEssentialsError (Error & { code }). It never throws and does not check instanceof Error. import { googleSignIn, isCredentialError, CredentialError } from 'react-native-oauth-essentials'; try { await googleSignIn(); } catch (e) { if (isCredentialError(e, CredentialError.CONFIGURATION_ERROR)) console.error(e.message); else if (isCredentialError(e)) report(e.code); else throw e; }

The library is a TurboModule, so importing it in Jest without a native module fails with a native module "OauthEssentials" was not found error. Use the mock shipped at react-native-oauth-essentials/jest.

Mock the library in a setup file referenced by setupFiles in your Jest config: // jest.setup.js (referenced by "setupFiles" in the Jest config) jest.mock('react-native-oauth-essentials', () => require('react-native-oauth-essentials/jest')); package.json { "jest": { "preset": "react-native", "setupFiles": ["./jest.setup.js"] } } You can also call the same jest.mock(...) at the top of a single test file.

Every method is a jest.fn() that resolves a plausible result: Method Resolves googleSignIn, googleSilentSignIn, hybridSignIn GOOGLE_ID with mock data (idToken: 'mock-google-id-token') appleSignIn APPLE_ID with mock data getPassword PASSWORD with { username: 'mock.user@example.com', password: 'mock-password' } createPassKey, getPassKey PASSKEY with a JSON string oauthSignIn OAUTH with code: 'mock-authorization-code' and the redirectUri you passed (or OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI) signOut, passwordSignIn true cancelPassKeyAutoFill false getAppleIdCredentialState AppleIdCredentialState.AUTHORIZED The listeners (addCredentialSuccessListener, addCredentialFailureListener, addAppleIdCredentialRevokedListener) are jest.fn() returning { remove: jest.fn() }. They never call your listener. The enums (CredentialsType, CredentialError, AppleIdCredentialState) and isCredentialError are the real ones. Every constant (GOOGLE_ID_SUPPORTED, PASSKEYS_SUPPORTED...) is true, and OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI is 'com.example.app://oauth/callback'.

import { googleSignIn, CredentialsType, CredentialError, } from 'react-native-oauth-essentials'; it('handles a cancelled Google sign in', async () => { (googleSignIn as jest.Mock).mockResolvedValueOnce({ type: CredentialsType.CANCELLED, data: null }); // render the screen and press the button... }); it('handles a browser error', async () => { (googleSignIn as jest.Mock).mockRejectedValueOnce( Object.assign(new Error('x'), { code: CredentialError.BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE }) ); // ... }); it('sends the client ids', async () => { // ... expect(googleSignIn).toHaveBeenCalledWith( { iosClientId: IOS_CLIENT_ID, webClientId: WEB_CLIENT_ID }, expect.objectContaining({ mode: 'button' }) ); }); Rejected errors need a code from CredentialError for isCredentialError to recognize them. To change a constant, mock the module with your own values: jest.mock('react-native-oauth-essentials', () => ({ ...require('react-native-oauth-essentials/jest'), PASSKEYS_SUPPORTED: false, }));

Every type, enum and type guard exported by react-native-oauth-essentials. Import types with import type, and enums and functions with a normal import: import { CredentialsType, CredentialError, isCredentialError } from 'react-native-oauth-essentials'; import type { GoogleIdCredentialResult, GoogleSignInOptions } from 'react-native-oauth-essentials'; The Platform column says where a property has an effect. Options that do nothing on the current platform are ignored, with a warning in development (see Development warnings). For the error codes, their causes and how to handle them, see Errors. Group Types Options GoogleClientIds, GoogleClientId, GoogleSignInOptions, HybridSignInOptions, AppleSignInOptions, PasskeyOptions, OAuthSignInOptions Results GoogleIdCredentialResult, PasswordCredentialResult, AppleIdCredentialResult, WebAppleIdCredentialResult, PassKeyCredentialResult, OAuthCredentialResult, CancelledCredentialResult, HybridSignInResult Events CredentialSuccessEvent, CredentialFailureEvent Enums CredentialsType, AppleIdCredentialState, CredentialError Errors CredentialErrorCode, OauthEssentialsError, isCredentialError

Method Resolves googleSignIn GoogleIdCredentialResult | CancelledCredentialResult googleSilentSignIn GoogleIdCredentialResult | CancelledCredentialResult signOut boolean (always true) getPassword PasswordCredentialResult | CancelledCredentialResult passwordSignIn boolean (saved or not; always false on iOS) appleSignIn AppleIdCredentialResult | WebAppleIdCredentialResult | CancelledCredentialResult getAppleIdCredentialState AppleIdCredentialState hybridSignIn HybridSignInResult createPassKey PassKeyCredentialResult | CancelledCredentialResult getPassKey PassKeyCredentialResult | CancelledCredentialResult cancelPassKeyAutoFill boolean (whether a pending AutoFill request was cancelled) oauthSignIn OAuthCredentialResult | CancelledCredentialResult addCredentialSuccessListener / addCredentialFailureListener / addAppleIdCredentialRevokedListener EventSubscription (from react-native, call .remove()) Every result has a type field from CredentialsType, so a switch (result.type) narrows data.

Google OAuth client ids per platform, all from the same Google Cloud project. Taken by googleSignIn, googleSilentSignIn and hybridSignIn. Both ids are optional: a missing id is read from the app config, which the Expo plugin writes from its options or the Firebase files (see Google client ids). type GoogleClientIds = { iosClientId?: string; webClientId?: string; }; Property Type Platform Description iosClientId string iOS iOS client id (created with the bundle id). When missing, iOS reads GIDClientID from Info.plist, then CLIENT_ID from the Firebase GoogleService-Info.plist. None rejects with CONFIGURATION_ERROR webClientId string Both Android: the client id passed to Credential Manager. When missing, Android reads the com.oauthessentials.GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID meta-data of AndroidManifest.xml, then the default_web_client_id string generated by the Firebase google-services Gradle plugin. None rejects with CONFIGURATION_ERROR. iOS: the default serverClientId (idToken audience and serverAuthCode); when missing, iOS reads GIDServerClientID from Info.plist

A GoogleClientIds object, or a single client id string. A string is used as is on both platforms, so it must be the iOS client id on iOS and the web client id on Android. type GoogleClientId = string | GoogleClientIds; // Ids in the app config (Expo plugin, Info.plist, AndroidManifest or Firebase files) await googleSignIn(); await googleSignIn({ mode: 'button' }); // Ids in code const GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS: GoogleClientIds = { iosClientId: '1234-abcd.apps.googleusercontent.com', webClientId: '5678-efgh.apps.googleusercontent.com', }; await googleSignIn(GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS, { mode: 'button' });

Options of googleSignIn and googleSilentSignIn. type GoogleSignInOptions = { authorizedAccounts?: boolean; autoSelectEnabled?: boolean; mode?: 'bottomSheet' | 'button'; nonce?: string; hint?: string; hostedDomain?: string; scopes?: string[]; offlineAccess?: boolean; serverClientId?: string; }; Property Type Default Platform Description authorizedAccounts boolean false Android Only show accounts that already signed in to the app autoSelectEnabled boolean false Android Sign in without UI when a single authorized account is available mode 'bottomSheet' | 'button' 'bottomSheet' Android bottomSheet shows the Credential Manager sheet and, unless authorizedAccounts is set, falls back to button when no credential is available (no account, or the sheet is in cooldown after being dismissed). button always shows the "Sign in with Google" flow: use it for a button tap nonce string - Both Embedded as is in the idToken, so your backend can prevent replay attacks. Ignored by googleSilentSignIn on iOS hint string - iOS Email to preselect in the Google page hostedDomain string - Both Restricts sign in to a Google Workspace domain. On Android it only applies to the button flow and to the authorization step, not to the bottom sheet scopes string[] - Both Additional OAuth scopes. iOS: requested during sign in; accessToken and grantedScopes are always returned. Android: requested in a second step (Authorization API, may show a consent screen); without scopes/offlineAccess, accessToken and grantedScopes are null offlineAccess boolean false Android Returns a serverAuthCode your backend can exchange for a refresh token. On iOS serverAuthCode is returned whenever serverClientId is set serverClientId string webClientId Both iOS: web (server) client id, used as the idToken audience and for serverAuthCode. Android: client id the serverAuthCode is issued for const options: GoogleSignInOptions = { mode: 'button', nonce: 'random-nonce', scopes: ['https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly'], }; await googleSignIn(options);

Options of hybridSignIn. Same shape as GoogleSignInOptions, but only some fields are used: type HybridSignInOptions = GoogleSignInOptions; Property iOS Android nonce Used, for Apple ID Used, for Google ID authorizedAccounts, autoSelectEnabled Ignored Used, for Google ID mode, hint, scopes, offlineAccess, hostedDomain, serverClientId Ignored Ignored

Options of appleSignIn. iOS only: on Android put the nonce and state in your androidWebUrl. type AppleSignInOptions = { nonce?: string; state?: string; }; Property Type Platform Description nonce string iOS Passed as is to Apple and embedded in the idToken. Firebase and Supabase expect the SHA-256 of the raw nonce here state string iOS Opaque value returned in AppleIdCredentialResult.data.state

Options of createPassKey and getPassKey. type PasskeyOptions = { requestJson: string; preferImmediatelyAvailableCredentials?: boolean; mediation?: 'modal' | 'autofill'; }; Property Type Default Platform Description requestJson string required Both WebAuthn options JSON from your server: PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions for createPassKey, PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions for getPassKey preferImmediatelyAvailableCredentials boolean false Android Only offer credentials already available on the device. iOS modal requests always behave this way mediation 'modal' | 'autofill' 'modal' iOS 16+ autofill (getPassKey only) shows passkeys in the QuickType bar of a text field with textContentType="username" instead of a sheet. See Passkeys const options: PasskeyOptions = { requestJson: JSON.stringify({ challenge: 'base64url-challenge', rp: { name: 'Your App', id: 'yourapp.com' }, user: { id: 'base64url-user-id', name: 'user@example.com', displayName: 'User Name' }, pubKeyCredParams: [{ type: 'public-key', alg: -7 }], authenticatorSelection: { userVerification: 'required' }, }), }; await createPassKey(options);

Options of oauthSignIn. type OAuthSignInOptions = { authorizationEndpoint: string; clientId: string; redirectUri?: string; scopes?: string[]; additionalParameters?: Record<string, string>; tokenEndpoint?: string; usePKCE?: boolean; prefersEphemeralSession?: boolean; }; Property Type Default Platform Description authorizationEndpoint string required Both Authorization url of the provider clientId string required Both OAuth client id redirectUri string OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI Both Where the provider redirects. Without a scheme it rejects with CONFIGURATION_ERROR scopes string[] - Both Sent as scope, space separated additionalParameters Record<string, string> - Both Extra authorization parameters, like prompt, login_hint or nonce. They may override scope. response_type, client_id, redirect_uri, state, code_challenge and code_challenge_method are set by the library and ignored here, with a warning in development tokenEndpoint string - Both When set, the code is exchanged for tokens on the device. Leave it out to exchange the code on your backend (recommended for confidential clients) usePKCE boolean true Both Sends a PKCE S256 code_challenge prefersEphemeralSession boolean false iOS Do not share cookies with Safari

Resolved by googleSignIn, googleSilentSignIn and hybridSignIn (Android). type GoogleIdCredentialResult = { type: CredentialsType.GOOGLE_ID; data: { id: string; idToken: string; displayName: string; givenName: string; familyName: string; email?: string; profilePictureUri?: string | null; phoneNumber?: string | null; accessToken?: string | null; serverAuthCode?: string | null; grantedScopes?: string[] | null; }; }; Field Type Platform Description id string Both iOS: Google user id (the idToken sub). Android: the account email idToken string Both JWT to verify on your backend displayName string Both Full name givenName string Both First name familyName string Both Last name email string Both Account email profilePictureUri string | null Both Profile picture url. iOS: 200px url, or "" without picture phoneNumber string | null Android Phone number, when shared accessToken string | null Both iOS: always returned. Android: only when scopes or offlineAccess were requested grantedScopes string[] | null Both Scopes granted to accessToken serverAuthCode string | null Both Android: with offlineAccess. iOS: when serverClientId (or webClientId) is set, never on googleSilentSignIn

Resolved by getPassword and hybridSignIn. type PasswordCredentialResult = { type: CredentialsType.PASSWORD; data: { username: string; password: string; }; }; Field Type Description username string Saved username or email password string Saved password

Resolved by appleSignIn and hybridSignIn on iOS. type AppleIdCredentialResult = { type: CredentialsType.APPLE_ID; data: { idToken: string; authorizationCode: string; user: string; email: string; fullName: string; likelyReal: boolean; state?: string | null; }; }; Field Type Description idToken string JWT to verify on your backend authorizationCode string Short lived code your backend can exchange with Apple user string Stable user id for the app (same across reinstalls). Pass it to getAppleIdCredentialState email string Email, possibly a private relay address. Apple only sends it on the first authorization fullName string Full name. Apple only sends it on the first authorization likelyReal boolean Apple considers the user likely a real person state string | null The state passed in AppleSignInOptions info Apple only sends email and fullName the first time a user authorizes the app. appleSignIn keeps the first result of each user in memory (until the app is killed) and fills them in later results, but save them on your backend on the first sign in.

Resolved by appleSignIn on Android, with the url your backend redirected to at the end of the Apple web flow. type WebAppleIdCredentialResult = { type: CredentialsType.WEB_APPLE_ID; data: { url: string; scheme: string | null; host: string | null; path: string | null; query: string | null; }; }; Field Type Description url string Full redirect url scheme string | null Url scheme, e.g. com.example.app host string | null Url host, e.g. oauth path string | null Url path, e.g. /callback query string | null Query string, with whatever your backend put there const params = new URLSearchParams(result.data.query ?? ''); const token = params.get('token');

Resolved by createPassKey and getPassKey. type PassKeyCredentialResult = { type: CredentialsType.PASSKEY; data: string; }; Field Type Description data string WebAuthn response JSON to send to your server: the registration response (createPassKey) or the authentication response (getPassKey), binary fields in base64url

Resolved by oauthSignIn. type OAuthCredentialResult = { type: CredentialsType.OAUTH; data: { code: string; state: string; redirectUri: string; codeVerifier: string | null; params: Record<string, string>; tokens: Record<string, unknown> | null; }; }; Field Type Description code string Authorization code state string The state generated by the library, already checked against the redirect redirectUri string Redirect uri used in the request. Send it with the code to your backend codeVerifier string | null PKCE verifier, null when usePKCE is false params Record<string, string> Every query and fragment parameter of the redirect tokens Record<string, unknown> | null Token endpoint JSON response, only when tokenEndpoint is set const result = await oauthSignIn({ authorizationEndpoint, clientId, scopes: ['openid', 'email'] }); if (result.type === CredentialsType.OAUTH) { await api.exchangeCode(result.data.code, result.data.codeVerifier, result.data.redirectUri); }

Resolved by every sign in method when the user dismisses the UI (and in the other cases listed per method in Methods). It is not an error: show the sign in screen again or other options. type CancelledCredentialResult = { type: CredentialsType.CANCELLED; data: null; };

Resolved by hybridSignIn. Apple ID only on iOS, Google ID only on Android. type HybridSignInResult = | AppleIdCredentialResult | GoogleIdCredentialResult | PasswordCredentialResult | CancelledCredentialResult;

Received by addCredentialSuccessListener. Same shape as the resolved result, including CANCELLED. type CredentialSuccessEvent = { type: string; data: Object; }; Field Type Description type string A CredentialsType value data object | null The result data (null for CANCELLED)

Received by addCredentialFailureListener. See which errors are emitted. type CredentialFailureEvent = { code: CredentialErrorCode; message: string; }; Field Type Description code CredentialErrorCode The error code message string Native error message

The type of every result. Value Result Resolved by GOOGLE_ID GoogleIdCredentialResult googleSignIn, googleSilentSignIn, hybridSignIn (Android) PASSWORD PasswordCredentialResult getPassword, hybridSignIn APPLE_ID AppleIdCredentialResult appleSignIn (iOS), hybridSignIn (iOS) WEB_APPLE_ID WebAppleIdCredentialResult appleSignIn (Android) PASSKEY PassKeyCredentialResult createPassKey, getPassKey OAUTH OAuthCredentialResult oauthSignIn CANCELLED CancelledCredentialResult Every sign in method const result = await hybridSignIn(); switch (result.type) { case CredentialsType.APPLE_ID: await api.signInWithApple(result.data.idToken); break; case CredentialsType.GOOGLE_ID: await api.signInWithGoogle(result.data.idToken); break; case CredentialsType.PASSWORD: await api.signIn(result.data.username, result.data.password); break; case CredentialsType.CANCELLED: showSignInScreen(); break; }

Resolved by getAppleIdCredentialState (iOS). Value Meaning What to do AUTHORIZED The user is still signed in to the app with Apple ID Nothing REVOKED The user stopped using Apple ID with the app Sign them out NOT_FOUND No credential for this user id Sign them out TRANSFERRED The app was transferred to another team Migrate the user id

The code of every rejection. Each code, its causes and how to handle it are in Errors. Value Meaning CONFIGURATION_ERROR The app is misconfigured (missing Google client id or URL scheme, invalid redirectUri) NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR The OS version, missing Play Services or the platform does not support the method NO_SIGN_IN_AVAILABLE There is no credential to return (no account, passkey or previous sign in) BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE The browser session could not be opened NO_ACTIVITY_ERROR No Android activity or iOS view controller to present the UI SIMULTANEOUS_CALL_ERROR iOS: the same method is still waiting for the previous call NETWORK_ERROR oauthSignIn: the token endpoint request failed INVALID_RESULT_ERROR The provider failed or returned something unexpected NO_PLAY_SERVICES_ERROR Deprecated, never used. Missing Play Services rejects with NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR

String union of the CredentialError values. Accepts both the enum members and their strings. type CredentialErrorCode = `${CredentialError}`; // 'CONFIGURATION_ERROR' | 'NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR' | 'NO_SIGN_IN_AVAILABLE' | ...

What the promises of the library reject with: an Error with a code. The native error text is in message. type OauthEssentialsError<C extends CredentialErrorCode = CredentialErrorCode> = Error & { code: C };

Type guard for catch blocks. Returns true when error is an object whose code is a CredentialError value, and equals code when given. It never throws. function isCredentialError<C extends CredentialErrorCode = CredentialErrorCode>( error: unknown, code?: C ): error is OauthEssentialsError<C>; import { googleSignIn, isCredentialError, CredentialError } from 'react-native-oauth-essentials'; try { await googleSignIn(); } catch (e) { if (isCredentialError(e, CredentialError.CONFIGURATION_ERROR)) console.error(e.message); else if (isCredentialError(e)) report(e.code, e.message); else throw e; }

Uses native AuthenticationServices framework Presents native Apple Sign-In UI sheet Full integration with iOS Keychain Returns complete user information on first sign-in Caches email and fullName in memory (until the app is killed) for subsequent sign-ins; store them on your backend Needs the Sign in with Apple capability (Expo: the config plugin appleSignIn: true option) Check APPLE_ID_SUPPORTED constant before using

Uses Custom Tabs to open your provided URL (options is ignored and logs a warning in development: put the nonce/state in your URL) Your backend must finish by redirecting to <applicationId>://oauth/callback (OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI) Returns redirect URL components after OAuth completion Requires backend implementation to handle OAuth flow You must implement Apple Sign-In REST API on your server See Apple Sign-In REST API Documentation Check APPLE_ID_SUPPORTED constant before using Implementation Note: iOS provides a complete native experience with full user data, while Android uses Chrome Custom Tabs to open your OAuth endpoint, then captures the redirect URL containing authorization data.

Initiates the Apple Sign-In process. Parameters​ Name Type Description androidWebUrl string (optional) The URL for Android OAuth flow. Required on Android, ignored on iOS. options AppleSignInOptions (optional) nonce (passed as-is to Apple; Firebase/Supabase expect its SHA-256) and state (iOS only, returned in data.state). Returns​ Promise<AppleIdCredentialResult | WebAppleIdCredentialResult> The promise resolves to different result types depending on platform: AppleIdCredentialResult (iOS): { type: CredentialsType.APPLE_ID; data: { idToken: string; // JWT ID token authorizationCode: string; // Authorization code for backend user: string; // Unique user identifier (stable) email: string; // User's email (only on first sign-in) fullName: string; // Full name (only on first sign-in) likelyReal: boolean; // Indicates if user is likely real state: string | null; // `options.state`, echoed back }; } WebAppleIdCredentialResult (Android): { type: CredentialsType.WEB_APPLE_ID; data: { url: string; // Full redirect URL from browser scheme: string | null; // URL scheme (e.g., "myapp") host: string | null; // URL host path: string | null; // URL path query: string | null; // URL query parameters containing auth code }; } Error Codes​ The method may throw errors with the following codes: Error Code Description Platform NO_ACTIVITY_ERROR No Android activity context available Android only BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE No browser available to open androidWebUrl Android only SIMULTANEOUS_CALL_ERROR Another Apple sign-in is still in progress iOS only INVALID_RESULT_ERROR Invalid URL parameter or authentication result Both The user cancelling the sheet resolves CANCELLED instead of throwing. iOS Implementation Details​ On iOS, the method: Presents the native Apple Sign-In UI sheet Returns complete user information on first sign-in only: email and fullName are only provided on first authorization Subsequent sign-ins return empty strings for these fields Caches email and fullName internally for future use The user identifier is stable across app reinstalls Use idToken for backend verification Use authorizationCode for server-to-server communication Important iOS Note: Apple only provides email and fullName once. The library caches these values, but you should store them in your backend on first sign-in. Android Implementation Details​ On Android, the method: Opens Chrome Custom Tabs with your androidWebUrl User completes OAuth flow in the browser Browser redirects to your app's deep link Returns the redirect URL components Your backend must: Serve the Apple Sign-In OAuth page Handle the OAuth flow Redirect back to your app with authorization code Verify the authorization code Important Android Note: You must implement the server-side Apple Sign-In flow. The library only handles opening the browser and capturing the redirect. Important Notes​ Always check APPLE_ID_SUPPORTED before calling this method On iOS: email/fullName only provided on first sign-in - cache them! On Android: androidWebUrl is required and must be implemented on your backend The flow and return types are completely different between platforms

Returns 'AUTHORIZED' | 'REVOKED' | 'TRANSFERRED' | 'NOT_FOUND' for the user returned by appleSignIn(). Apple recommends checking it on every app launch and signing the user out when it is not AUTHORIZED. Rejects with NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR on Android.

Called when the user stops using Apple ID with your app while it is running. const subscription = addAppleIdCredentialRevokedListener(() => signOutLocally()); // later subscription.remove(); Example Usage (TypeScript)​ import { appleSignIn, APPLE_ID_SUPPORTED, CredentialsType, Platform, } from 'react-native-oauth-essentials'; async function signInWithApple(): Promise<void> { if (!APPLE_ID_SUPPORTED) { console.log('Apple Sign-In is not supported on this platform.'); return; } try { const credential = await appleSignIn( Platform.OS === 'android' ? 'https://yourserver.com/auth/apple' : undefined ); if (credential.type === CredentialsType.APPLE_ID) { // iOS: Native Apple Sign-In result console.log('iOS Apple Sign-In:'); console.log('User ID:', credential.data.user); console.log('ID Token:', credential.data.idToken); console.log('Auth Code:', credential.data.authorizationCode); console.log('Email:', credential.data.email || 'Not provided (subsequent sign-in)'); console.log('Name:', credential.data.fullName || 'Not provided (subsequent sign-in)'); console.log('Likely Real:', credential.data.likelyReal); // Send to your backend for verification await authenticateWithBackend({ idToken: credential.data.idToken, authCode: credential.data.authorizationCode, user: credential.data.user, email: credential.data.email, fullName: credential.data.fullName, }); } else if (credential.type === CredentialsType.WEB_APPLE_ID) { // Android: Redirect URL from browser OAuth flow console.log('Android Apple Sign-In:'); console.log('Redirect URL:', credential.data.url); console.log('Query params:', credential.data.query); // RECOMMENDED: Extract short-lived session code from your backend const sessionCode = extractSessionCode(credential.data.query); // Exchange session code for credentials with your backend const authResult = await exchangeSessionCode(sessionCode); console.log('Authenticated:', authResult); // ALTERNATIVE (less secure): Extract auth code directly // const authCode = extractAuthCode(credential.data.query); // await exchangeAuthCode(authCode); } } catch (error) { if (error.code === CredentialError.NO_ACTIVITY_ERROR) { console.error('Activity context not available'); } else if (error.code === CredentialError.INVALID_RESULT_ERROR) { console.error('Invalid authentication result'); } else { console.error('Apple Sign-In failed:', error); } } } // Helper function for Android - Extract session code (RECOMMENDED) function extractSessionCode(query: string | null): string { if (!query) throw new Error('No query parameters'); const params = new URLSearchParams(query); const sessionCode = params.get('session_code'); // Your backend sends this if (!sessionCode) throw new Error('No session code in redirect'); return sessionCode; } // Exchange session code for credentials (RECOMMENDED) async function exchangeSessionCode(sessionCode: string) { const response = await fetch('https://yourserver.com/api/auth/apple/exchange', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ session_code: sessionCode }), }); return await response.json(); } // ALTERNATIVE (less secure): Extract authorization code directly function extractAuthCode(query: string | null): string { if (!query) throw new Error('No query parameters'); const params = new URLSearchParams(query); const code = params.get('code'); // Apple authorization code if (!code) throw new Error('No authorization code in redirect'); return code; }

Enable Sign in with Apple: Add Sign in with Apple capability to your App ID in Apple Developer Portal Enable the capability in Xcode project settings (it adds com.apple.developer.applesignin = ["Default"] to the entitlements). With Expo, set "appleSignIn": true in the config plugin instead The library handles all native implementation Backend Token Verification (Recommended): Verify the idToken on your backend server See Apple: Sign in with Apple REST API Use Apple's token verification endpoint

Backend Implementation Required: Implement Apple Sign-In OAuth flow on your server Serve an OAuth authorization page at your androidWebUrl Handle the callback from Apple Redirect back to your app with authorization code See Apple Sign-In REST API Documentation Deep Link Setup: Configure a deep link scheme in your AndroidManifest.xml Handle incoming deep links from the browser The library captures the redirect URL automatically Recommended Secure Backend Flow: User clicks sign in → App opens Chrome Custom Tabs with your URL → Your server shows Apple OAuth page → User authorizes with Apple → Apple redirects to your server callback with authorization code → Your server generates a SHORT-LIVED session code (expires in 60s) → Your server redirects to your app deep link with the session code → App receives redirect URL with session code (NOT credentials) → App posts session code to your backend → Your backend validates session code and returns credentials Security Benefit: This avoids exposing sensitive credentials or authorization codes through the deep link URL, which could be intercepted or logged. Alternative (Less Secure) Flow: If you cannot implement the session code flow, you can send the authorization code directly via deep link, but this is less secure: → Your server redirects to deep link with authorization code → App extracts code from query parameters → App immediately sends code to backend for token exchange

Besides resolving or rejecting, the sign in methods report their result through events. Use them for things that are not tied to one call site: analytics, logging, or reacting to an Apple ID being revoked while the app runs. Every listener returns an EventSubscription. Call remove() when you no longer need it (e.g. on unmount).

Called with the same { type, data } the promise resolves with, including CANCELLED. Emitted by googleSignIn, googleSilentSignIn, getPassword, appleSignIn, hybridSignIn, createPassKey and getPassKey. Not emitted by signOut, passwordSignIn, getAppleIdCredentialState, cancelPassKeyAutoFill and oauthSignIn. The event type is a CredentialsType value and data is the result data (see CredentialSuccessEvent).

Called with { code, message } when one of the methods above rejects, including CONFIGURATION_ERROR from the Google and hybrid methods (see CredentialFailureEvent; code is typed as CredentialErrorCode). oauthSignIn never emits, so its NETWORK_ERROR and CONFIGURATION_ERROR only reject. These rejections are not emitted: SIMULTANEOUS_CALL_ERROR iOS passkey NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR (below iOS 16) iOS passkey call without requestJson On Android, passwordSignIn resolves false on errors (including the user declining), which emits nothing. getPassword resolves CANCELLED when the user dismisses it or there is no saved password (emitted as a success event) and rejects with INVALID_RESULT_ERROR on other errors (emitted as a failure event).

Called when iOS posts ASAuthorizationAppleIDProvider.credentialRevokedNotification: the user stopped using Apple ID with your app (Settings > Apple ID > Sign in with Apple) while the app is running. Sign the user out when it fires. Never called on Android. It only covers revocations while the app runs. Also call getAppleIdCredentialState on app start.

import { useEffect } from 'react'; import { addCredentialSuccessListener, addCredentialFailureListener, addAppleIdCredentialRevokedListener, CredentialsType, } from 'react-native-oauth-essentials'; export function useAuthEvents(signOutLocally: () => void) { useEffect(() => { const subscriptions = [ addCredentialSuccessListener((event) => { if (event.type !== CredentialsType.CANCELLED) { analytics.track('sign_in', { method: event.type }); } }), addCredentialFailureListener((event) => { analytics.track('sign_in_error', { code: event.code, message: event.message }); }), addAppleIdCredentialRevokedListener(() => signOutLocally()), ]; return () => subscriptions.forEach((subscription) => subscription.remove()); }, [signOutLocally]); } caution The success event carries the full result, including Google/Apple tokens and saved passwords. Do not send event.data to analytics or logs.

Uses the GoogleSignIn SDK, which opens the Google page in an ASWebAuthenticationSession Presented from the top most view controller; waits up to 2 seconds for the app to become active No Google Play Services dependency GOOGLE_ID_SUPPORTED is always true Uses iosClientId (or GIDClientID from Info.plist, then CLIENT_ID of GoogleService-Info.plist) and webClientId as the default serverClientId (or GIDServerClientID from Info.plist) Needs the reversed iOS client id as a URL scheme in Info.plist; without it the call rejects with CONFIGURATION_ERROR

Minimum: Android 7.0 (API 24, the library minSdk) Uses Credential Manager (GetGoogleIdOption bottom sheet or GetSignInWithGoogleOption button flow) and, for scopes/offlineAccess, the Authorization API Requires Google Play Services: without them it rejects with NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR. GOOGLE_ID_SUPPORTED equals GOOGLE_PLAY_SERVICES_SUPPORTED Uses webClientId (or the com.oauthessentials.GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID manifest meta-data, then the Firebase default_web_client_id string); without any the call rejects with CONFIGURATION_ERROR Supports additional options: mode, authorizedAccounts and autoSelectEnabled

Performs Google ID sign-in on Android and iOS platforms. Also callable as googleSignIn() and googleSignIn(options) when the client ids are in the app config (the simplest setup). Parameters​ Name Type Description clientId string | { iosClientId?: string; webClientId?: string } (optional) Your Google client ids. Omit it to read them from the app config. See Client ids. options GoogleSignInOptions (optional) Optional configuration for Google Sign-In. See GoogleSignInOptions for details. Client ids​ From the app config (recommended). Call googleSignIn() or googleSignIn(options) and the native side reads the ids from the app (the Expo config plugin writes them, from its options or the Firebase files): iOS: GIDClientID in Info.plist, then CLIENT_ID of the Firebase GoogleService-Info.plist bundled in the app. serverClientId (idToken audience and serverAuthCode) defaults to GIDServerClientID. Android: the com.oauthessentials.GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID meta-data in AndroidManifest.xml, then the default_web_client_id string generated by the Firebase google-services Gradle plugin. See Installation for the native snippets. With no id anywhere, the call rejects with CONFIGURATION_ERROR (the message lists the sources). In code. Pass { iosClientId, webClientId } (type GoogleClientIds), all from the same Google Cloud project. A passed id wins over the config, and a missing one is read from it: iOS uses iosClientId. webClientId becomes the default serverClientId. Android uses webClientId. The Android client id is never passed: it only has to exist with your package name and SHA-1 fingerprints. An object with iosClientId or webClientId is the client ids; any other object is the options. A string still works and is used as is: it must be the iOS client id on iOS and the web client id on Android. Pass null to give options explicitly without client ids. GoogleSignInOptions​ type GoogleSignInOptions = { authorizedAccounts?: boolean; // Android only: Filter to authorized accounts autoSelectEnabled?: boolean; // Android only: Enable auto-selection mode?: 'bottomSheet' | 'button'; // Android only: UI flow (default 'bottomSheet') nonce?: string; // Embedded as-is in the idToken (replay protection) hint?: string; // iOS only: Email to preselect hostedDomain?: string; // Workspace domain (Android: button flow and authorization only) scopes?: string[]; // Extra OAuth scopes offlineAccess?: boolean; // Android only: returns serverAuthCode serverClientId?: string; // iOS: idToken audience + serverAuthCode (default webClientId). Android: serverAuthCode client id }; mode: 'button' should be used when the user taps a "Sign in with Google" button. bottomSheet falls back to it automatically when no credential is available, unless authorizedAccounts is set. scopes and offlineAccess trigger an extra consent step on Android (Authorization API). Declining it resolves CANCELLED. On iOS scopes are requested during sign in, and accessToken/grantedScopes are always returned. serverAuthCode is returned whenever serverClientId is set (offlineAccess has no effect). Options that have no effect on the current platform log a console.warn in development. See Methods for the exact per-platform behavior. Returns​ Promise<GoogleIdCredentialResult | CancelledCredentialResult> The promise resolves to: GoogleIdCredentialResult: { type: CredentialsType.GOOGLE_ID; data: { id: string; // iOS: Google user id (sub). Android: account email idToken: string; // JWT ID token for backend verification displayName: string; // Full name givenName: string; // First name familyName: string; // Last name email?: string; // Email profilePictureUri?: string | null; // Profile picture URL phoneNumber?: string | null; // Android only accessToken?: string | null; // iOS: always. Android: when `scopes`/`offlineAccess` is set serverAuthCode?: string | null; // iOS: when `serverClientId` is set. Android: when `offlineAccess` is set grantedScopes?: string[] | null; // Same as accessToken }; } CancelledCredentialResult: { type: CredentialsType.CANCELLED; data: null; // User cancelled the sign-in flow } Error Codes​ The method may throw errors with the following codes: Error Code Description Platform CONFIGURATION_ERROR No client id passed nor found in the app config (see Client ids), or the iOS URL scheme is missing from Info.plist (the message has the exact scheme) Both NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR Google Play Services not available or outdated Android only NO_ACTIVITY_ERROR No activity / view controller to present from Both NO_SIGN_IN_AVAILABLE No Google account available for the requested filter (iOS: googleSilentSignIn only) Both BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE The sign-in page could not be opened (app not active within 2 s, Guided Access, Safari restricted) iOS only SIMULTANEOUS_CALL_ERROR googleSignIn/googleSilentSignIn is still pending iOS only INVALID_RESULT_ERROR The provider failed or returned an unexpected result Both Important Notes​ Check GOOGLE_ID_SUPPORTED before calling this method (on Android it is false without Play Services) The idToken should be sent to your backend for verification Options mode, authorizedAccounts and autoSelectEnabled only work on Android User can cancel the flow, resulting in CancelledCredentialResult Use idToken's sub claim (verified on your backend) as the user id: data.id differs between platforms Example Usage (TypeScript)​ import { googleSignIn, isCredentialError, GOOGLE_ID_SUPPORTED, CredentialsType, CredentialError, } from 'react-native-oauth-essentials'; const GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS = { iosClientId: 'YOUR_IOS_CLIENT_ID.apps.googleusercontent.com', webClientId: 'YOUR_WEB_CLIENT_ID.apps.googleusercontent.com', }; async function signInWithGoogle(): Promise<void> { // Android: false without Google Play Services if (!GOOGLE_ID_SUPPORTED) { console.log('Google sign-in is not available on this device.'); return; } try { const credential = await googleSignIn(GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS, { authorizedAccounts: true, // Android only autoSelectEnabled: false, // Android only }); if (credential.type === CredentialsType.GOOGLE_ID) { console.log('Signed in with Google:'); console.log('ID Token:', credential.data.idToken); console.log('User ID:', credential.data.id); console.log('Name:', credential.data.displayName); console.log('Email:', credential.data.email); // Send idToken to your backend for verification await authenticateWithBackend(credential.data.idToken); } else if (credential.type === CredentialsType.CANCELLED) { console.log('User cancelled Google sign-in'); } } catch (error) { if (isCredentialError(error, CredentialError.CONFIGURATION_ERROR)) { console.error('Setup problem:', error.message); // e.g. the iOS URL scheme to add } else if (isCredentialError(error, CredentialError.NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR)) { console.error('Please install or update Google Play Services'); } else if (isCredentialError(error, CredentialError.BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE)) { console.error('Could not open the Google page, try again'); } else if (isCredentialError(error, CredentialError.NO_ACTIVITY_ERROR)) { console.error('Activity context not available'); } else { console.error('Google sign-in failed:', error); } } }

Hybrid sign-in is a user-friendly approach that combines the best of native and app-level authentication. It relies entirely on the platform's built-in sign-in methods, giving users a seamless and familiar experience and making the app feel like a world-class app. A good UX is to dispatch hybrid sign-in immediately on app start. If any error occurs or user cancels, fall back to a custom UI with your desired authentication flow. ⚠️ Important: Users cannot choose the platform methods - the OS presents available credentials Android: Google ID must be configured (webClientId, passed or in the app config). iOS: the client id is ignored, Google is not offered Always handle the CANCELLED case - users may dismiss the credential picker We highly recommend using hybrid sign-in as the default for unauthenticated users, while still providing alternative sign-in options to cover all cases.

Offers: Apple ID and saved passwords (ASAuthorizationController). Google ID is not included On iOS 16+ only credentials already on the device are offered Resolves CANCELLED when the user dismisses it or nothing is available Only options.nonce is used (for Apple ID); the client id and other options log a warning in development Ideal for app launch to restore previous session

Offers: Google ID (GetGoogleIdOption) and saved passwords. Apple ID is not included (use appleSignIn()) Uses Credential Manager to aggregate the options in one bottom sheet Requires Google Play Services: rejects with NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR without them (HYBRID_SUPPORTED is false then) Uses webClientId, or the web client id from the app config (manifest meta-data or Firebase); rejects with CONFIGURATION_ERROR without any authorizedAccounts, autoSelectEnabled and nonce are used; mode, hint, scopes, offlineAccess, hostedDomain and serverClientId are ignored (with a warning in development)

Performs all available sign-in methods on the platform at once. Also callable as hybridSignIn() and hybridSignIn(options) when the web client id is in the app config. This is typically used on app startup to retrieve any existing sign-in credentials. Parameters​ Name Type Description clientId GoogleClientId (optional) Same as googleSignIn: { iosClientId, webClientId } or a string, or omitted to read it from the app config. Android uses webClientId; ignored on iOS. See Google client ids. options GoogleSignInOptions (optional) Optional configuration for Google Sign-In. See GoogleSignInOptions for details. GoogleSignInOptions​ type GoogleSignInOptions = { authorizedAccounts?: boolean; // Android only: Filter to authorized accounts autoSelectEnabled?: boolean; // Android only: Enable auto-selection nonce?: string; // Android: Google idToken nonce. iOS: Apple ID nonce }; Other GoogleSignInOptions fields are ignored by hybridSignIn. Returns​ Promise<AppleIdCredentialResult | GoogleIdCredentialResult | PasswordCredentialResult | CancelledCredentialResult> The promise resolves to whichever credential is available on the platform: GoogleIdCredentialResult (Android only): { type: CredentialsType.GOOGLE_ID; data: { id: string; idToken: string; displayName: string; givenName: string; familyName: string; profilePictureUri?: string | null; phoneNumber?: string | null; }; } AppleIdCredentialResult (iOS only): { type: CredentialsType.APPLE_ID; data: { idToken: string; authorizationCode: string; user: string; email: string; fullName: string; likelyReal: boolean; }; } PasswordCredentialResult: { type: CredentialsType.PASSWORD; data: { username: string; password: string; }; } CancelledCredentialResult: { type: CredentialsType.CANCELLED; data: null; // User dismissed the credential picker } Error Codes​ Error Code Description Platform CONFIGURATION_ERROR No webClientId Android only NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR Google Play Services not available or outdated Android only NO_ACTIVITY_ERROR No Android activity context available Android only NO_SIGN_IN_AVAILABLE No Google account or saved password for the request Android only SIMULTANEOUS_CALL_ERROR A previous hybridSignIn is still pending iOS only INVALID_RESULT_ERROR The provider failed or returned an unexpected result Both Important Notes​ Check HYBRID_SUPPORTED before using hybrid sign-in: always true on iOS, same as GOOGLE_PLAY_SERVICES_SUPPORTED on Android On iOS, Apple ID and stored passwords may be returned On Android, Google ID and stored passwords may be returned (Apple requires separate Chrome Custom Tabs flow) Useful for automatically signing in users if credentials are already available User can cancel, resulting in CancelledCredentialResult Options authorizedAccounts and autoSelectEnabled only work on Android Emits onCredentialSuccess / onCredentialFailure Example Usage (TypeScript)​ import { hybridSignIn, HYBRID_SUPPORTED, CredentialsType, } from 'react-native-oauth-essentials'; const GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS = { iosClientId: 'YOUR_IOS_CLIENT_ID.apps.googleusercontent.com', webClientId: 'YOUR_WEB_CLIENT_ID.apps.googleusercontent.com', }; async function initAuth(): Promise<void> { if (!HYBRID_SUPPORTED) { console.log('Hybrid sign-in is not supported on this platform.'); // Show manual sign-in UI return; } try { const credential = await hybridSignIn(GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS, { authorizedAccounts: true, // Android only autoSelectEnabled: false, // Android only }); switch (credential.type) { case CredentialsType.GOOGLE_ID: console.log('Signed in with Google:', credential.data.displayName); await authenticateWithBackend('google', credential.data.idToken); break; case CredentialsType.APPLE_ID: console.log('Signed in with Apple ID:', credential.data.user); await authenticateWithBackend('apple', credential.data.idToken); break; case CredentialsType.PASSWORD: console.log('Signed in with stored password:', credential.data.username); await authenticateWithBackend('password', credential.data.username, credential.data.password); break; case CredentialsType.CANCELLED: console.log('User cancelled credential picker'); // Show manual sign-in UI break; } } catch (error) { console.error('Hybrid sign-in failed:', error); // Show manual sign-in UI } }

Perfect for restoring user session when app starts: async function handleAppLaunch() { try { const credential = await hybridSignIn(GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS); if (credential.type !== CredentialsType.CANCELLED) { // User has existing credentials, auto sign-in await processCredential(credential); navigateToHomeScreen(); } else { // No credentials or user cancelled, show sign-in screen navigateToSignInScreen(); } } catch (error) { console.error(error); // Error occurred, show sign-in screen navigateToSignInScreen(); } }

Show a single button that tries all methods: async function handleContinueButton() { try { const credential = await hybridSignIn(GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS); if (credential.type === CredentialsType.CANCELLED) { // User dismissed, show other sign-in options showAlternativeSignInOptions(); return; } // Process the credential await processCredential(credential); } catch (error) { console.error(error); showAlternativeSignInOptions(); } }

Call on app start - Try hybrid sign-in immediately when app launches for authenticated users Handle cancellation - Users may dismiss the credential picker, show alternative options Fallback to manual UI - Always provide manual sign-in options if hybrid fails Check support constants - Verify HYBRID_SUPPORTED before calling Don't repeat - If user cancels, don't immediately call hybrid again Fast UX - Hybrid sign-in is instant, perfect for app startup Platform differences - iOS includes Apple ID, Android doesn't (requires separate flow)

Go to home screen navigateToHomeScreen(); } else { // Backend rejected, show sign-in screen navigateToSignInScreen(); } } catch (error) { console.error('Hybrid sign-in error:', error); navigateToSignInScreen(); } }
