Using the built-in password sign-in features is much more secure than storing usernames and passwords manually. Android and iOS keep saved credentials cryptographically secure, and when synced (e.g., via Google Password Manager on Android or iCloud Keychain on Apple devices), they can be accessed across your devices. This makes signing in with a username and password take only a few seconds. You can check more on following links: Apple Support - iCloud Keychain - Details how Apple keeps passwords secure and synced across devices. Google Chrome Developers - Passkeys and Google Password Manager - Explains how Google encrypts and syncs passwords and passkeys on Android and other devices.

Minimum: iOS 12+ Uses iOS Keychain Services Integrates with iCloud Keychain for sync across devices Presents native password autofill UI Supports AutoFill everywhere Matches saved passwords through the webcredentials:yourdomain.com Associated Domain (see Passkeys, or the Expo plugin webCredentialsDomains option) Check PASSWORD_SUPPORTED constant before using

Minimum: Android 7.0+ (API 24+) Uses Credential Manager API Integrates with Google Smart Lock for Passwords Can sync credentials across devices via Google account Presents native credential picker UI Supports autofill everywhere Requires Google Play Services: PASSWORD_SUPPORTED equals GOOGLE_PLAY_SERVICES_SUPPORTED, and the methods reject with NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR without them Check PASSWORD_SUPPORTED constant before using

Always start by calling getPassword to try retrieving saved credentials automatically. If it resolves CANCELLED or fails, show your own login UI for the user to enter their username and password. Validate these credentials on your backend, and once your backend returns the API credentials, store the same username/password using the passwordSignIn method so that future sign-ins can happen automatically. Android and iOS keep saved credentials cryptographically secure and synced across devices, making sign-in fast and safe.

Retrieves a previously stored password credential from the device. Parameters​ This function does not take any parameters. Returns​ Promise<PasswordCredentialResult | CancelledCredentialResult> PasswordCredentialResult: { type: CredentialsType.PASSWORD; data: { username: string; // Stored username password: string; // Stored password }; } Resolves to a PasswordCredentialResult object when the user picks a stored credential. Resolves to { type: CredentialsType.CANCELLED, data: null } when the user dismisses it or no stored password is found, on both platforms. It never resolves false. Migrating to 1.1 Before 1.1, Android resolved false when there was no password or on errors. Replace if (!result) / result === false checks with result.type === CredentialsType.CANCELLED. Other Android errors now reject with INVALID_RESULT_ERROR. Error Codes​ Error Code Description Platform NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR Google Play Services not available or outdated Android only NO_ACTIVITY_ERROR No Android activity context available Android only SIMULTANEOUS_CALL_ERROR A previous getPassword is still pending iOS only INVALID_RESULT_ERROR Invalid result from credential manager Both Notes​ Always check PASSWORD_SUPPORTED before calling this method Available on both Android (API 24+) and iOS (12+) Useful for retrieving credentials that were previously saved via the password manager Resolves CANCELLED if no credential is stored (not an error) Example Usage (TypeScript)​ import { getPassword, PASSWORD_SUPPORTED, CredentialsType } from 'react-native-oauth-essentials'; async function retrievePassword(): Promise<void> { if (!PASSWORD_SUPPORTED) { console.log('Password sign-in is not supported on this platform.'); return; } try { const credential = await getPassword(); if (credential.type === CredentialsType.CANCELLED) { console.log('No stored password found or the user dismissed it.'); // Show manual login UI return; } if (credential.type === CredentialsType.PASSWORD) { console.log('Retrieved password credential'); console.log('Username:', credential.data.username); // Authenticate with your backend await authenticateWithBackend( credential.data.username, credential.data.password ); } } catch (error) { console.error('Failed to get stored password:', error); // Show manual login UI } }

Saves username/password credentials to the platform's credential manager. Parameters​ Name Type Description username string The username of the account. password string The password for the account. Returns​ Promise<boolean> Resolves to true if credentials are successfully saved (Android) Resolves to false if saving fails or the user declines (Android), and always on iOS, where it does nothing (it logs a warning in development): use textContentType on your inputs so iOS offers to save the password Error Codes​ Error Code Description Platform NOT_SUPPORTED_ERROR Google Play Services not available or outdated Android only NO_ACTIVITY_ERROR No Android activity context available Android only Notes​ Always check PASSWORD_SUPPORTED before calling this method The password cannot be a previously stored credential retrieved via getPassword Only call this method after successful backend authentication Available on both Android (API 24+) and iOS (12+) The credential will be synced via iCloud Keychain (iOS) or Google Password Manager (Android) Example Usage (TypeScript)​ import { passwordSignIn, PASSWORD_SUPPORTED } from 'react-native-oauth-essentials'; async function signInWithPassword(username: string, password: string): Promise<void> { if (!PASSWORD_SUPPORTED) { console.log('Password sign-in is not supported on this platform.'); return; } try { // First authenticate with your backend const authSuccess = await authenticateWithBackend(username, password); if (!authSuccess) { console.log('Invalid credentials'); return; } // Save credentials to credential manager for future auto sign-in const saved = await passwordSignIn(username, password); if (saved) { console.log('Credentials saved successfully - will auto sign-in next time'); } else { console.log('Failed to save credentials - will need to sign in manually next time'); } } catch (error) { console.error('Password sign-in error:', error); } }

Always try getPassword() first - Check for stored credentials before showing login UI Only save after backend validation - Don't save credentials until your backend confirms they're valid Handle the CANCELLED case gracefully - getPassword() resolving CANCELLED is normal, not an error Sync benefits - Saved credentials work across all user's devices via iCloud/Google sync Security - Credentials are encrypted and stored securely by the OS Combine with biometrics - Consider adding biometric authentication for extra security

async function handleAuth() { // 1. Try to get saved credentials first const saved = await getPassword(); if (saved.type === CredentialsType.PASSWORD) { // Auto sign-in with saved credentials await authenticateWithBackend(saved.data.username, saved.data.password); return; } // 2. No saved credentials, show login UI const { username, password } = await showLoginUI(); // 3. Authenticate with backend const success = await authenticateWithBackend(username, password); if (success) { // 4. Save credentials for next time await passwordSignIn(username, password); } }
Stored in iOS Keychain (highly secure) Synced via iCloud Keychain to all user's Apple devices Supports AutoFill in Safari and WKWebView Integrated with Face ID / Touch ID prompts

Uses Credential Manager API Synced via Google Password Manager to all user's devices with same Google account Supports AutoFill framework in apps and browsers Can prompt for device authentication (PIN/fingerprint/face)

oauthSignIn signs in with any OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect provider (Microsoft, GitHub, Facebook, Auth0, Keycloak, your own server...) using the authorization code flow with PKCE, in a secure browser session.
Uses ASWebAuthenticationSession The redirect scheme does not need to be registered in Info.plist prefersEphemeralSession disables cookie sharing with Safari

Uses Chrome Custom Tabs The redirect must reach the library CustomTabsActivity. OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI (<applicationId>://oauth/callback) already does; for another uri, add an intent filter for it to com.oauthessentials.CustomTabsActivity in your AndroidManifest.xml

Parameters​ Name Type Description authorizationEndpoint string Provider authorization url clientId string Your OAuth client id redirectUri string? Defaults to OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI scopes string[]? Requested scopes additionalParameters Record<string, string>? Extra authorization parameters, like prompt. May override scope; state, redirect_uri, code_challenge and the other parameters set by the library are ignored tokenEndpoint string? Exchanges the code for tokens on the device usePKCE boolean? Defaults to true prefersEphemeralSession boolean? iOS only Returns​ Promise<OAuthCredentialResult | CancelledCredentialResult> OAuthCredentialResult.data has the authorization code, state, redirectUri, the PKCE codeVerifier, every redirect parameter in params and, with tokenEndpoint, the token response in tokens. The state is generated and verified by the library. A provider access_denied error resolves as CANCELLED; other provider errors, and a non JSON token response, reject with INVALID_RESULT_ERROR. When the browser cannot be opened it rejects with BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE, when the token request fails (offline, DNS, TLS...) with NETWORK_ERROR, and when redirectUri has no scheme with CONFIGURATION_ERROR. Every rejection has a code: narrow it with isCredentialError. oauthSignIn does not emit events. Example: exchange the code on your backend (recommended)​ import { oauthSignIn, OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI, CredentialsType } from 'react-native-oauth-essentials'; const result = await oauthSignIn({ authorizationEndpoint: 'https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0/authorize', clientId: 'YOUR_CLIENT_ID', scopes: ['openid', 'profile', 'email', 'offline_access'], }); if (result.type === CredentialsType.OAUTH) { await api.post('/auth/microsoft', { code: result.data.code, codeVerifier: result.data.codeVerifier, redirectUri: result.data.redirectUri, // must match OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI registered in the provider }); } Example: public client token exchange on the device​ const result = await oauthSignIn({ authorizationEndpoint: 'https://your-tenant.auth0.com/authorize', tokenEndpoint: 'https://your-tenant.auth0.com/oauth/token', clientId: 'YOUR_CLIENT_ID', scopes: ['openid', 'profile'], }); if (result.type === CredentialsType.OAUTH) { console.log(result.data.tokens?.access_token); } Never put a client secret in the app: providers that require one (GitHub OAuth apps, Facebook) must exchange the code on your backend.

Passkeys are a modern, secure way for users to sign in using biometric authentication (Face ID, Touch ID) or device PIN. They work across devices when synced via iCloud (iOS) or Google Password Manager (Android).

Minimum: iOS 16+ Uses native AuthenticationServices framework Presents native passkey creation/selection UI Full integration with iCloud Keychain Supports Face ID, Touch ID, and device PIN Check PASSKEYS_SUPPORTED constant before using

Minimum: Android 9.0+ (API 28+) Uses Credential Manager API with passkey support Presents native passkey creation/selection UI Integrates with Google Password Manager Supports biometric and device authentication Check PASSKEYS_SUPPORTED constant before using

1. Add Associated Domains Capability​ To use passkeys on iOS, you must add the Associated Domains capability to your app: Open your Xcode project Select your target and go to Signing & Capabilities tab Click + Capability button Search for and add Associated Domains In the Associated Domains section, add your domain in this format: webcredentials:yourdomain.com With Expo, use the config plugin instead: "webCredentialsDomains": ["yourdomain.com"] adds webcredentials:yourdomain.com (merged with your existing associated domains). 📚 Reference: See Apple's guide on adding capabilities to your app for detailed instructions. 2. Configure your Domain​ Your backend domain must host an apple-app-site-association file at: https://yourdomain.com/.well-known/apple-app-site-association This file tells Apple that your app is allowed to use passkeys from your domain: { "webcredentials": { "apps": [ "TEAM_ID.BUNDLE_ID" ] } } Replace: TEAM_ID with your Apple Team ID BUNDLE_ID with your app's bundle identifier 3. Use the Correct Domain in Your Code​ When creating or asserting passkeys, the rp.id (relying party ID) must match your configured domain: const options = { requestJson: JSON.stringify({ challenge: 'your-challenge', rp: { id: 'yourdomain.com', // Must match your Associated Domain name: 'Your App Name' }, user: { id: 'user-id', name: 'user@yourdomain.com', displayName: 'User Name' }, pubKeyCredParams: [{ type: 'public-key', alg: -7 }], timeout: 60000, attestation: 'none', authenticatorSelection: { authenticatorAttachment: 'platform', userVerification: 'preferred' } }) };

Android 9+ uses the Credential Manager API. Nothing to add to the app, but the rp.id domain must declare your app with a Digital Asset Links file at: https://yourdomain.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json [ { "relation": [ "delegate_permission/common.handle_all_urls", "delegate_permission/common.get_login_creds" ], "target": { "namespace": "android_app", "package_name": "com.yourcompany.yourapp", "sha256_cert_fingerprints": [ "AA:BB:CC:..." ] } } ] Replace: package_name with your applicationId sha256_cert_fingerprints with the SHA-256 of every signing key: debug, release and the Play App Signing key (Play Console > Setup > App signing). cd android && ./gradlew signingReport prints the debug and release ones Without it Credential Manager refuses the request for that rp.id and the method rejects. Your backend must also validate the passkey responses.

Creates a new passkey credential. Parameters​ Name Type Description options PasskeyOptions Passkey creation configuration Returns​ Promise<PassKeyCredentialResult> PassKeyCredentialResult: { type: CredentialsType.PASSKEY; data: string; // JSON string containing the public key credential response } Example Usage​ import { createPassKey, PASSKEYS_SUPPORTED, CredentialsType } from 'react-native-oauth-essentials'; async function registerPasskey(): Promise<void> { if (!PASSKEYS_SUPPORTED) { console.log('Passkeys are not supported on this platform.'); return; } try { const credential = await createPassKey({ requestJson: JSON.stringify({ challenge: await getServerChallenge(), rp: { id: 'yourdomain.com', name: 'Your App' }, user: { id: 'user-id', name: 'user@yourdomain.com', displayName: 'User Display Name' }, pubKeyCredParams: [{ type: 'public-key', alg: -7 }], timeout: 60000, attestation: 'none', authenticatorSelection: { authenticatorAttachment: 'platform', userVerification: 'preferred' } }) }); if (credential.type === CredentialsType.PASSKEY) { const passkeyData = JSON.parse(credential.data); console.log('Passkey created successfully'); // Send to your backend for verification await verifyPasskeyWithBackend(passkeyData); } } catch (error) { console.error('Failed to create passkey:', error); } }

Retrieves an existing passkey credential for authentication. Parameters​ Name Type Description options PasskeyOptions Passkey retrieval configuration Returns​ Promise<PassKeyCredentialResult> Example Usage​ import { getPassKey, PASSKEYS_SUPPORTED, CredentialsType } from 'react-native-oauth-essentials'; async function authenticateWithPasskey(): Promise<void> { if (!PASSKEYS_SUPPORTED) { console.log('Passkeys are not supported on this platform.'); return; } try { const credential = await getPassKey({ requestJson: JSON.stringify({ challenge: await getServerChallenge(), rpId: 'yourdomain.com', timeout: 60000, userVerification: 'preferred' }) }); if (credential.type === CredentialsType.PASSKEY) { const passkeyData = JSON.parse(credential.data); console.log('Passkey authentication successful'); // Send to your backend for verification await verifyPasskeyWithBackend(passkeyData); } } catch (error) { console.error('Failed to authenticate with passkey:', error); } }

Pass mediation: 'autofill' to show the user's passkeys in the QuickType bar of the username field instead of a modal sheet. Start the request when the sign in screen mounts; the promise only settles when the user picks a passkey or the request is cancelled. The username TextInput must have textContentType="username" and autoComplete="username". import { useEffect } from 'react'; import { TextInput } from 'react-native'; import { getPassKey, cancelPassKeyAutoFill, CredentialsType } from 'react-native-oauth-essentials'; function SignInScreen() { useEffect(() => { getPassKey({ requestJson: JSON.stringify(requestOptions), mediation: 'autofill' }) .then((credential) => { if (credential.type === CredentialsType.PASSKEY) { verifyPasskeyWithBackend(JSON.parse(credential.data)); } }) .catch(console.error); return () => { cancelPassKeyAutoFill(); }; }, []); return <TextInput textContentType="username" autoComplete="username" />; } A modal getPassKey or createPassKey call cancels the pending AutoFill request, which resolves as CANCELLED. On Android mediation is ignored and cancelPassKeyAutoFill resolves false.

Always check PASSKEYS_SUPPORTED before calling passkey methods Use the correct domain in rp.id - it must match your Associated Domain (iOS) Store challenges securely on your backend and never reuse them Validate attestations on your backend to ensure passkey authenticity Handle errors gracefully - users may cancel or lack passkey support Use biometric verification - passkeys are secure because they require user verification Test thoroughly - test on physical devices with real passkeys
